title: How Reading Changes the Way Your Brain Works
content: Reading is unnatural. This will hardly come as a surprise to any child trying to put off his homework for just one more hour of watching other kids play Minecraft. Yet there really are implications worth considering if we accept that our cognitive systems didn’t evolve to process text in the same way as they evolved to handle vision and speech. Speaking on an evolutionary historical scale, “we haven’t had enough time to develop a dedicated reading brain,” says UCLA neuroscientist Rebecca Gotlieb in the BBC World Service video above. For the time being, in a kind of cognitive jerry-rigging, “we co-opt parts of the brain involved in vision and auditory processing and language and attention and affect.”

title: Ignore human rights risks, face the consequences: Telenor under investigation for crimes against humanity in Myanmar
content:
On September 15, 2026, Norwegian authorities announced an investigation into Telenor for suspected crimes against humanity and sanctions violations in Myanmar following the 2021 military coup. For years, Access Now and civil society have raised the alarm over Telenor’s hasty and irresponsible departure from Myanmar and the potential human rights abuses should Telenor sell its Myanmar enterprise to the military-linked M1 Group.

The decision to file charges against Telenor follows a police complaint filed by Justice for Myanmar and ICJ Norway last year. Earlier this year, the Swedish human rights group Justice and Accountability Initiative (JAI), with the support of various Myanmar civil society organizations and EU-based groups, also filed a class-action lawsuit against Telenor.

In August 2021, Access Now, along with 44 organizations, laid out the potential dangers of this sale to the Telenor board, calling for it to stop the sale and conduct human rights due diligence in line with international standards. Telenor responded on September 3, 2021. Ultimately, Telenor refused to listen to civil society and proceeded with the sale.

title: California’s “Addictive Feeds” Law Violates Teens’ First Amendment Rights
content:
A California law that prohibits teens from receiving recommended social media content from other social media users violates their First Amendment rights, EFF argued this week.

The case, Meta v. Bonta, challenges SB 976, which requires that teen social media users get their parents’ permission before seeing other users’ recommended speech on their social media feeds. The legal challenge to SB 976 has largely centered on how the law violates social media services’ First Amendment rights to curate user-generated content and present it as they see fit.

But the friend-of-of the-court brief EFF filed along with the Center for Democracy & Technology and the Wikimedia Foundation shows that the law violates teen users’ First Amendment rights, too.

“SB 976 frustrates young people’s ability to use the internet to its full potential, prohibiting them from relying on tools that disseminate their speech and help them view and interact with other users’ speech,” the brief argues.

Recommendation systems have a dual purpose on social media: they help all users discover speech and content by other users, and to get their own speech in front of a wider audience.
snippet: A California law that prohibits teens from receiving recommended social media content from other social media users violates their First Amendment rights, EFF argued this week.

title: Pragmatic principles for more rights-respecting age assurance architectures
content:
This is the second part of a two-part series in which we explore approaches to protecting children online while safeguarding privacy, security and the open web. Part one covers our concerns regarding age gates, and suggests alternative policy proposals that address the root causes of online harms. Part two explores better ways to build age assurance architectures that respect users’ rights and autonomy.

Across the world, legislation to introduce age gates and social media bans is proliferating. Many governments are still considering age restrictions a straight-forward and cost-effective tool to achieve their child safety goals. However, evidence is mounting that age assurance mandates pose risks to users’ privacy, security, free expression and access to  information, threaten the open web and competition, and undermine policymakers’ goals: enabling young people to have safe and trustworthy experiences online, while enabling the digital economy to grow.

title: AI titans invited to Trump-Xi dinner
content:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon plan to attend next week’s state dinner with President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, four people familiar with the event told POLITICO.

The executives’ attendance at the White House summit signals artificial intelligence will likely be a key talking point during negotiations and comes as fear the technology could destroy humanity has roiled the industry.

An OpenAI spokesperson, who confirmed Altman’s attendance, did not detail his goals for the summit and instead pointed to his recent comments that the two leaders could earn a Nobel Peace Prize if they reach a deal on AI. Another person, who was granted anonymity to speak on details not yet made public, confirmed Huang’s attendance, but did not provide details on his goals for the summit.

Amon, whose attendance was confirmed by a Qualcomm spokesperson, said the CEO will represent the company and “the strength of American technology leadership on the global stage.”

Anthropic declined to comment on whether it received an invitation. Spokespeople for Google, Meta and AMD did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

Editor’s note: This article is  based on a presentation and interview with Russian street artist Slava PTRK , originally from Yekaterinburg, Russia, who currently lives abroad, in exile. title: Woman Executed at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan
content:
According to HRANA, a prisoner was executed at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan at dawn on Monday, September 14, 2026.

HRANA has identified the prisoner as Rezvan Asgharzadeh, a 45-year-old mother of six. On Sunday evening, one day before her execution, she was transferred from Dowlatabad Prison in Isfahan to Dastgerd Prison.

According to information received by HRANA, Asgharzadeh was arrested approximately six years and six months ago in connection with drug-related offenses. About two years ago, Branch 5 of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hemmat-Nejad, sentenced her to death. The sentence was subsequently upheld by the Supreme Court.

An informed source close to her family told HRANA: “During her imprisonment, Ms. Asgharzadeh memorized several sections of the Quran in hopes of qualifying for clemency, and until her final days she remained hopeful that her sentence would be commuted. Her name was initially included on the list of prisoners eligible for clemency. However, following a negative report submitted by Fatemeh Asgarian, the head of Dowlatabad Prison in Isfahan, her name was removed from the list.”

title: US Revokes Limits on Power Plants’ Climate Pollution
content:
The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced on September 14 that it is repealing limits on climate-warming pollution from coal and gas-fired power plants, the second largest source of greenhouse gas emissions in the country.

By gutting the 2024 Carbon Pollution Standards, the EPA is eliminating most of the limits on power plants’ carbon emissions. The move is one of the Trump administration’s most significant attacks yet on the US government’s ability to confront the climate crisis and protect communities devastated by pollution.

The 2024 standards required existing coal plants and new gas plants to capture 90 percent of carbon emissions or shut down by 2039, which would have reduced carbon pollution by an estimated 1.38 billion metric tons through 2047. The Biden-era rule was also projected to help reduce power plants’ emissions of health-harming pollutants, including sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, and fine particulate matter.

title: Embodied Freedom and Mutual Recognition: A Fichtean Foundation for Healthcare Ethics
content:
By Sam Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 17 September 2026 (IDN) — Beauchamp and Childress’ principlist framework has shaped biomedical ethics for more than four decades, providing clinicians and policymakers with a vocabulary centered on autonomy, beneficence, nonmaleficence, and justice. Its influence is undeniable: the four principles have become the default language of ethics committees, medical school curricula, and institutional policy.

Yet principlism’s strength—its broad flexibility and intuitive appeal—is also its deepest weakness. Designed as a “mid-level” approach that avoids metaphysical or theoretical commitments, principlism cannot provide a foundational account of healthcare ethics. Its principles lack justification beyond a shifting and often contested “common morality”; it offers no ontology of the human person; it cannot adjudicate conflicts among its own norms; and it reduces autonomy to little more than procedural respect for patient choice. Such limitations have long been acknowledged yet rarely addressed at their philosophical root.

title: The Guardian view on the Nepal-Tibet floods: a spur to action on climate | Editorial
content:
New research links last month’s disaster to fossil fuel pollution. Supporting disaster-hit countries must be at the centre of climate politics

Following a familiar pattern, coverage of the glacier collapse on the Nepal-Tibet border three weeks ago has subsided with the initial shock. But while the world’s attention has shifted, Nepal remains in the midst of an appalling tragedy. As well as at least 1,300 people who are known to have been killed, more than 5,000 are missing, some of them trapped in tunnels linked to the 13 hydropower plants that were damaged by the floods. On Wednesday four bodies were recovered from one of these tunnels, with searches ongoing. Families of the missing people are desperate for news.

title: Europe heard Draghi. Now it has to act
content:
The report by Mario Draghi, The Future of European Competitiveness, published on 9 September 2024, was intended as a response to the widening gap between the European economy and its US and Chinese competitors.

The former president of the European Central Bank pointed to low productivity, insufficient investment in new technologies, high energy prices, fragmentation of the single market and difficulties in financing European companies.

Draghi called for a deeper single market, simpler regulation, better access to finance and the mobilisation of additional public and private investment. He estimated that the EU needed around €750–800 billion in additional investment every year — equivalent to 4.4–4.7% of EU GDP — to finance the transition and restore economic dynamism.

Two years later, the core of Draghi’s diagnosis has been broadly accepted in Brussels. The implementation of his prescriptions, however, tells a much less impressive story.

title: IJ4EU Impact Award 2026 winners announced
content:
Two investigations into deadly “forever chemicals” are among the three winners of the 2026 IJ4EU Impact Awards, alongside a cross-border exposé showing how doctors sanctioned for malpractice are able to continue working after being banned elsewhere.

The winning teams of journalists each received €5,000 at the annual awards presented by the Investigative Journalism for Europe (IJ4EU) fund, which supports cross-border public-interest journalism in Europe.

In alphabetical order, the three equal winners are:

  • Bad Practice, by a consortium of 50 media outlets led by OCCRP, VG and The Times.
  • Factories on the Run: Inside the Global Trade that Moves PFAS Downstream, by Gianluca Liva, Marta Frigerio, Anna Violato, Filippo Tommasoli, Thomas Goorden and Varrun Sukhraj.
  • The Forever Lobbying Project, by a consortium of European media partners coordinated by Le Monde.

    • The jury also singled out Killing for the Photo, by Barbara Matejčić in collaboration with Natalija Jovanović and Ruben Brugnera, for special recognition.

    The winners were announced on September 17 in Budapest at IJ4EU’s annual UNCOVERED Conference, hosted this year by Goethe-Institut Hungary.

title: ‘Doom Loop’: OpenAI and Microsoft Admits LLMs Are Destroying the Web and Built on Theft
content:
Executives working on AI at Microsoft and OpenAI admitted what its critics have been saying all along: Large language models are predatory pieces of technology that have been built on what a Microsoft executive called “an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions,” and the “largest theft of labor in human history.” An internal Microsoft document said generative AI products have created a “doom loop” that is killing “the entire web.” 

Those statements and a series of other mask-off moments feature heavily in an unredacted court filing that was unsealed Thursday in the behemoth New York Times vs OpenAI copyright lawsuit that has been winding its way through the court system for years. In a filing asking for summary judgment (basically, a filing with the court asking it to rule), lawyers for the New York Times laid out a series of admissions made by Microsoft and OpenAI executives in documents and depositions that until now had remained either sealed or redacted at the request of Microsoft and OpenAI.

title: Six Convicted, €300M Confiscation Ordered in Mafia-Linked EU Tax Fraud
content:
A Milan court has sentenced six individuals to prison and ordered the confiscation of more than 300 million euros ($344.66 million) for their roles in a transnational tax fraud and money laundering syndicate tied to the Italian mafia, the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) announced on Thursday.

The convictions mark the latest judicial actions in "Operation Moby Dick," a massive EPPO investigation into a VAT carousel fraud scheme. Between 2020 and 2023, the network issued over 1.3 billion euros ($1.49 billion) in fake invoices for AirPods, laptops, and other electronics, resulting in 520 million euros ($597.35 million) in losses to EU and national budgets.

The Milan judge confirmed aggravated circumstances for the criminal syndicate’s aiding and abetting of a mafia association. According to the EPPO, one of the convicted defendants received illicit funds from a Camorra clan—which investigators previously linked to the Nuvoletta and Di Lauro groups—and funneled the money into the scheme to launder the mafia's proceeds.

title: Oregon Lawmakers Seek to Open Up Affordable Housing Records Following ProPublica’s Reporting
content:
Two Oregon lawmakers want to end an unusual exemption in the state’s records law that has kept the public from learning how hundreds of millions of dollars in taxpayer money is spent on subsidized housing — and the effort has already landed key industry support.

Rep. Pam Marsh, chair of Oregon’s House Committee on Housing and Homelessness, told ProPublica that she plans to introduce legislation next year to eliminate a law that shields key details of state spending on low-income housing.

The southern Oregon Democrat said she didn’t realize the documents were being kept secret until reading about it in a ProPublica story. She said previous leaders of her committee told her they were also unaware.

“I think this is an issue that will have very broad interest,” Marsh said.

State Sen. Khanh Pham, a Portland Democrat and chair of the Senate Committee on Housing and Development, said she also wants the Legislature to tackle the issue in its next session.

title: Esittävän taiteen tukirakenteiden kehitysprosessi on käynnistynyt
content:
Joukko esittävän taiteen järjestöjä ja muita alan tukirakenteita on käynnistänyt keväällä 2026 yhteisen kehitystyön kohti tulevaisuuskestävää esittävän taiteen ekosysteemiä ja vaikuttavampaa yhteistoimintaa.

Järjestöt tunnistavat siiloutumisen ja ovat huolissaan siitä, miten jatkuvasti heikentyneet voimavarat riittävät tehtävien ja tarkoituksen toteuttamiseen. Kehitystyön ytimessä onkin kysymys, millaiset tukirakenteet palvelevat esittävää taidetta ja sen uudistumista sekä taiteentekijöiden moninaisen toimijakentän tarpeita pitkällä tähtäimellä – rakenteellisesti kestävällä tavalla.

Kehitysprosessi mahdollistaa keskenään erilaisten toimijoiden säännöllisen yhteen tulemisen ja yhteisen ajattelun. Työssä yhtä aikaa kerätään ja jäsennetään tietoa sekä kokeillaan ja kehitetään syntyviä ideoita käytännössä.

Esittävän taiteen järjestö- ja tukirakenteita edustavat yhteisöt osallistuvat kehitystyöhön kukin omista lähtökohdistaan ja tarpeistaan käsin. Prosessi on sen osallistujayhteisöille mahdollisuus vahvistaa yhteyttä kollegoihin ja luoda suhteita muihin toimijoihin samalla kun ymmärrys esittävän taiteen kentän tilannekuvasta ja omasta toiminnasta osana kokonaisuutta tarkentuu.

title: Humanitarian Archive Emergency Coalition: Get Involved Remotely!
content:
The DRP has been pleased to be part of a growing coalition concerned about the future of humanitarian archives amid challenges to foreign aid funding. 

In response to these concerns, a Steering Committee from around the world was convened by researchers at the University of Manchester’s Humanitarian and Conflict Response Institute and launched as the Humanitarian Archive Emergency Coalition. In addition to creating a Registry to document at-risk archives, the HAE has created a Digital Archiving Toolkit, a Landscape Report, and more. 

They’ve also been running five in-person regional workshops around the world to gather feedback from practitioners, archivists, researchers, and custodians. They will be conducting several online workshops at the end of the month and welcome more participation. Join one of three online workshops (2 hours each) based on your preferred language and time zone:

  • English – Tuesday 29 September, 12:00 CET (10:00 UTC)
  • French – Wednesday 30 September, 16:00 CET (14:00 UTC / 10:00 Port-au-Prince)
  • Spanish – Thursday 1 October, 10:00 EST (14:00 UTC / 09:00 Panama)

title: Vallan maantiede: Ovatko Yhdysvaltojen terveysdiilit syöttö Kiinan lapaan?
content:
Vuosi sitten Yhdysvaltojen hallinto julkaisi uuden strategian globaalin terveyden edistämiseksi. Strategiapaperin otsikkoon oli liitetty tuttu iskulause ”Amerikka ensin”. Samassa yhteydessä strategian toimeenpano siirrettiin terveysministeriöstä ulkoministeriöön.

Pian strategian julkistamisen jälkeen Trumpin hallinto lähestyi Afrikan maita. Se halusi nyt neuvotella kahdenvälisiä diilejä – aiesopimuksia, jotka mahdollistaisivat terveysavun jatkamisen, mutta entistä tiukemmilla ehdoilla.

Yhdysvalloille ei riittänyt pelkästään se, että jatkossa kehitysapuvarojen käyttöä syynättäisiin tarkemmin. Avun vastineeksi se halusi suoran pääsyn afrikkalaisten terveysdataan ja patogeeninäytteisiin, jopa mineraaleihin.

Mutta mikä on hinta sille, jos globaalia terveysapua ohjaavat ensisijaisesti Yhdysvaltojen intressit? Intressit, jotka ovat yhä useammin kaupallisia, tai ulko- ja turvallisuuspoliittisia.

Ja mitä riskejä sisältyy siihen, että Yhdysvallat vetäytyy monenkeskisestä yhteistyöstä, ja rakentaa rinnalle omia järjestelmiään, joissa sen edut menevät yhteisen terveysturvallisuuden edelle?

Huomataanko uusi pandemia ajoissa?

Vallan maantiede -podi julkaistaan yhteistyössä Maailman Kuvalehden kanssa.

title: The End Of Upward Mobility
content: In April 1941, with the Wehrmacht in Paris and the Ribbentrop–Molotov pact still in force, the political theorist James Burnham published “The Managerial Revolution,” which famously declared that capitalism was finished. His claim was not that it ought to be finished, but that it was, as a matter of observable fact, being replaced. The successor system would not, however, be socialism, as he had hoped during his earlier days as a Trotskyist. Socialism, he argued, was a utopia: it required abundance, and since human wants are unlimited, abundance is unreachable.

title: Houthi advance boosts Iran’s leverage over the US and Saudi Arabia – but may cost rebel group its legitimacy back in Yemen
content:
It took just a few days for Houthi forces to seize most of Yemen’s Red Sea coast, including the shores of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial Red Sea maritime choke point.

The offensive started on Sept. 3, 2026, with a push to cut the strategically important road linking the city of Taiz to the port of Mokha. By Sept. 11, Mokha, the town of Dhubab and the island of Mayyun, in the mouth of the strait, were under Houthi control.

The Yemeni rebel group seized some 2,100 square miles of territory, forcing more than 100,000 people to flee, according to the U.N., with many making the risky journey to nearby Djibouti by boats.

It is the largest shift in the front lines of Yemen’s civil war since a U.N.-brokered truce froze them in April 2022.

Most of the coverage has interpreted the offensive as a new lever for Iran – a key ally of the Houthis – in its ongoing war with the United States, or a fresh threat to Saudi Arabia and global shipping.

title: Erdogan muutti mielensä, hakee jatkokautta Turkin johdossa
content:
Turkin presidentti Recep Tayyip Erdogan aikoo hakea jatkokautta presidentinvaaleissa, jotka järjestetään todennäköisesti vuoden 2028 huhtikuussa, kertoo hänen avustajansa turkkilaismedian mukaan.

Vielä vuonna 2023 edellisvaalien aikaan Erdogan sanoi, että alkava viisivuotiskausi jäisi hänen viimeisekseen. Erdogan (s. 1954) on ollut Turkin presidenttinä vuodesta 2014 alkaen.

Normaaliaikataulun mukaan seuraavat vaalit järjestettäisiin toukokuussa, mutta maan parlamentin odotetaan aikaistavan niitä järjestettäväksi 16. huhtikuuta.

Uutistoimisto AFP:n ja uutissivusto al-Monitorin mukaan päätös sallisi Erdoganin hakea jatkokautta.

Hallitus väitti aiemmin, ettei vaalien aikaistaminen ollut sen suunnitelmissa.

title: Vihreiden Mikkonen ja Pitko: Suomen tärkein luontopäätös valmistellaan pimennossa
content:
Hallitus salailee Suomen ennallistamissuunnitelman valmisteluja, kritisoivat vihreiden kansanedustajat Krista Mikkonen ja Jenni Pitko. Esimerkiksi Suomen suurin luontotyyppi, pohjoiset havumetsät, on poistettu nyt suunnitelmasta kokonaan.

Lisäksi lausuntokierrokselle lähetettiin kesällä muiden luontotyyppien, kuten soiden ja vesistöjen, osalta vain tiivistelmä, ei koko suunnitelmaa eikä vaikutusten arviota, mikä tekee Pitkon mukaan asiallisen lausunnon antamisen lähes mahdottomaksi.

He vaativat EU:lle valmisteilla olevalle suunnitelmaluonnokselle kunnollista lausuntokierrosta.

"Hallitus on lähettämässä komissiolle suunnitelman, jossa ei ole kerrottu, miten Suomi tulee varmistamaan luonnon tilan elpymisen ja luontokadon pysäyttämisen. Suunnitelmassa on metsien kohdalla tyhjä rivi, vaikka pitkälti metsissä ratkaistaan luontomme monimuotoisuus, sillä kolmasosa uhanalaisista lajeistamme ovat metsälajeja", korostaa Krista Mikkonen tiedotteessa.

"Kyse on Suomen suurimmasta luontotyypistä ja tärkeimmästä luontoa koskevasta päätöksestä vuosikymmeniin. Silti sen tulevaisuudesta päätetään suljettujen ovien takana. Tämä ei ole avointa lainvalmistelua, vaan sen vastakohta", Pitko sanoo.

title: EU leaders visited Arktikum as a part of the European Arctic Summit held in Rovaniemi
content:
17.09.2026

  • Share on FaceBook
  • Share on LinkedIn

    • The European Arctic Summit was held in Rovaniemi 13-14 September 2026, where EU leaders gathered to address issues related to the Arctic region.

    The geopolitical significance of the Arctic continues to grow rapidly, and the aim of the European Arctic Summit held in Rovaniemi was to strengthen the EU’s common strategic approach to the region. Arktikum served as a meeting venue for the summit, where the EU leaders also got to visit the Arctic Opposites science exhibition by the Arctic Centre with the executive producer Nicolas Gunslay.

    In addition, EU politicians discussed with local representatives about current Arctic questions such as the impacts of climate change and the perspectives of the Sámi People’s, the EU’s only Indigenous People, to the changing state of the region. The Rector of the University of Lapland Antti Syväjärvi and the President of the Sámi Parliament of Finland Pirita Näkkäläjärvi took part in these discussions held in Arktikum. The President Näkkälärvi emphasized to European heads of state that sustainable Arctic security can’t be achieved without the people of the Arctic and vibrant Indigenous peoples.

title: The next frontier for circularity is governance
content: Resource extraction has tripled since 1970, and on current trends, it could rise by a further sixty per cent by 2060 against 2020 levels. This will exacerbate the planetary crisis and drive economic risk, including price volatility and supply chain disruption. Linear waste, materials extracted, used once and discarded, costs the global economy €25.4 trillion a year, close to a third of global GDP. While circularity was expected to counter this trajectory, the Circle Economy’s Circularity Gap Report puts the world’s circularity rate at 6.9 per cent, the lowest figure the metric has recorded since its introduction in 2018.

title: Documenting Lampung’s Living Heritage: Inside WikiNgigel
content:
Traditional dance and music are not simply performances. They are living forms of cultural knowledge, carried through movement, music, memory, teaching, and community practice. Yet much of this knowledge remains difficult to discover online, particularly when it comes to high-quality audiovisual documentation that can be freely accessed, studied, reused, and connected to other forms of knowledge.

In Lampung, Indonesia, WikiNgigel was created to help address this gap.

Implemented by Komunitas Wikimedia Bandar Lampung through a Wikimedia Foundation Rapid Fund project, WikiNgigel focuses on documenting Lampung’s traditional dance and musical traditions and bringing that documentation into the Wikimedia ecosystem. The project combines field documentation, collaboration with cultural practitioners, Wikimedia Commons, Wikipedia, Wikimedia Incubator, community training, and public dissemination.

The project began from a simple observation: documenting cultural heritage is not only about creating photographs or videos. It is also about making sure that the resulting documentation becomes useful knowledge.

title: Kasvipohjaiset maitotuotteiden vaihtoehdot pääosin turvallisia, mutta lisää tutkimusta tarvitaan
content:
Suomessa kaupan olevat kasvipohjaiset maitotuotteiden vaihtoehdot ja vegaaniset jälkiruoat ovat elintarviketurvallisuudeltaan pääosin laadukkaita. Ruokaviraston ja VTT:n VEGETURVA-hankkeessa tehdyn riskinarvioinnin mukaan tuotteiden mikrobiologiset riskit olivat yleisesti vähäisiä ja tutkittujen mykotoksiinien pitoisuudet jäivät määritysrajan alle. Samalla tulokset osoittavat, että kuluttajien säilytyskäytännöillä, tuotteiden raaka-aineilla ja eräiden haitta-aineiden esiintymisellä voi olla merkitystä turvallisuuden kannalta.

Kasvipohjaisten maitotuotteiden vaihtoehtojen käyttö on viime vuosina lisääntynyt nopeasti. Vaikka niiden ravitsemuksellisia ominaisuuksia on tutkittu paljon, turvallisuudesta on ollut saatavilla selvästi vähemmän tietoa. Ruokaviraston ja VTT:n yhteistyössä toteutetussa VEGETURVA-hankkeessa selvitettiin kasvijuomien, kasvipohjaisten jogurttityyppisten tuotteiden sekä vegaanisten jälkiruokien mikrobiologisia ja kemiallisia riskejä sekä tuotteiden käyttöön liittyviä turvallisuuskysymyksiä.

title: Symposium: Indigenous Relationships with Time
content:
The MultiBEING Justice Centre of Excellence will kick-off at the University of Helsinki. CoE organizes its first scientific symposium on Monday September 28th, 2026 and engages with Indigenous notions of time by distinguished international speakers. 

The symposium addresses the connections and lineages of beings. Conceptions of time shape how relationships with other beings are lived, valued, and perceived. Non-linear time is a key aspect of understanding Indigenous relational onto-epistemologies. The speakers foreground philosophies of time, seasonalities, traditional calendars, ancestralities, astronomy, and diverse temporalities and timelines. What role do they play in reconsidering multibeing flourishing and human responsibility beyond humans?

title: Ten Heritage Projects in N. Mexico Receive Funding
content:
The Heritage Management Organization (HERITΛGE) is delighted to announce the 10 projects selected to receive funding through HerMaP Mexico, its major initiative to strengthen cultural heritage management across Mexico’s northern border region.

The selected projects represent Baja California, Sonora, Chihuahua, Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas, ensuring that all six states within HerMaP Mexico’s geographic scope are represented in this first round of funding.

The projects were chosen from 115 applications submitted through an open call launched in early 2026, demonstrating both the extraordinary richness of the region’s cultural heritage and the commitment of communities, practitioners and institutions working to safeguard it. 

The selected initiatives offer a window onto the remarkable diversity of northern Mexico. They encompass heritage ranging from traditional farming techniques and gastronomic traditions to crafts, music, memorial sites, museums and the photographic documentation of intangible cultural heritage. They are rooted in landscapes that stretch from ocean coasts and vast deserts to mountain regions and complex urban environments.

Fri entré.

Varmt välkommen på vernissage lördagen den 17/10 kl. 13.00 i konstnärens närvaro!Samma dag invigs den nya barnavdelningen på Finlandsinstitutets bibliotek. Utställningen är öppen för publiken mellan kl. 11 och 15 på lördag.

Matias Karsikas glaskonst visas i oktober–november även i en utställning på Galleri Glas i Stockholm. Utställningen Tusen sjöars glöd öppnar den 22/10. Läs mer om utställningen hos Galleri Glas.

I oktober öppnar utställningen Nord i blom med den finska skulptören Matias Karsikas i Finlandsinstitutets galleri. I utställningen presenteras Karsikas blomsterinspirerande glasskulpturer samt ett ryaliknande verk i keramik, en teknik som är karakteristisk för konstnären.

Naturen är ett återkommande tema i Matias Karsikas arbete. Konstnären är särskilt intresserad av spänningen mellan naturen och den den mänskligt skapade världen. För Karsikas framstår naturen inte som en romantisk idyll, utan som en kontinuerlig process av överlevnad, skörhet och motståndskraft på samma gång.

title: An In-Depth, Immersive Journey Through the Bayeux Tapestry
content:
With the Bayeux Tapestry now on display at the British Museum, Deep Down History presents a deep dive into the embroidery’s full story:

“The Bayeux Tapestry is one of the most remarkable survivals of the Middle Ages — a 70 metre embroidered account of the events leading to the Norman Conquest of England in 1066, culminating in the Battle of Hastings. This video tells the Tapestry’s story in full, using Charles Stothard’s early colour reproduction, presented here as a seamless scroll for the first time. We follow Harold Godwinson’s fateful journey from Edward the Confessor’s court to Normandy, his later seizure of the Crown, and William the Conqueror’s invasion. Beyond its political messaging, the Tapestry is also bursting with medieval history, including jokes, fascinating technical details, and a warning for those who break their promises…”

Enjoy!

title: Parents, privacy, parliaments: The battle begins for von der Leyen’s social media ban
content:
BRUSSELS — Ursula von der Leyen’s bill to keep young Europeans off social media is an ambitious response to the growing outcry over the potential harm of TikTok, Instagram and other online platforms. Making the restrictions a reality will require a whole new level of ambition.

The European Commission must now negotiate with national governments and technologists to figure out exactly how to impose a law across Europe that would ban kids under 13 from social media, and severely restrict access for those under 15 — all without trampling on privacy of young and old alike in the process of verifying users’ age. 

Reducing the harms of social media on youth has been a top priority for the Commission president, a medical doctor and mother of seven who has repeatedly decried the internet’s impact on the health of minors since her 2025 State of the Union speech.  

“If a platform wants to access the children or the teenagers, the minors, they have to prove first that they are safe,” she told reporters on Thursday as she officially unveiled the EU Kids Act, the day after again touting her leadership on the issue in this year’s annual address.

title: Global: Women Human Rights Defenders take their fight to the UN during week-long advocacy meeting
content:
Women Human Right Defenders (WHRDs) from around the world will be gathering in Geneva from 21 to 25 September, to learn about the UN Human Rights Council, advocate for their rights and amplify their own stories.

The week-long training, known as the Women Human Rights Advocacy Week, is co-organized by nine human rights organizations including Amnesty International (see below for full list). It is aimed at providing participants with practical tools to understand the Human Rights Council, while offering guidance on how to engage with it strategically and advocate for change in their communities.

“The women attending are risking their lives every day to protect their communities from climate change, greedy corporations and land theft,” said Lisa Maracani, Amnesty International’s researcher on human rights defenders. “Their knowledge is crucial to ensuring bodies such as the Human Rights Council remain effective, while the WHRD Advocacy Week is designed to provide these women with the tools and strategies to advance their advocacy on this global stage.”

title: The long journey from ‘Indigenous’ to citizen in Mozambique
content:
From “Indigenous” to achieving citizenship, the story of resistance, transformation, and rights in Mozambique.

Originally published on Global Voices

Photo taken by Speak Media Uganda. Used under the Pexels license.

Under the Portuguese Empire (roughly 1505 until 1975), the word “Indigenous” was not just a descriptive word for the African population of Mozambique. It was a legal category that determined rights, duties, and life possibilities. For Africans in Mozambique — including communities such as the Ronga, Changan, and others in the region — the colonial experience was characterized by deep inequality before the state. Being African and born in Mozambique did not entail being treated as a citizen with the same rights as a European.

The Portuguese colonial system established a distinction between the “Indigenous,” “assimilated,” and  Portuguese citizens. Most of the African population remained in the category “Indigenous.” Access to formal education, qualified employment, public administration, and other opportunities was much more limited. The education system particularly revealed this inequality.

From “Indigenous” to achieving citizenship, the story of resistance, transformation, and rights in Mozambique.

title: Satire Can be a Crime in Kazakhstan
content:
Satirist and political commentator Azamat Omarov, who had been in pre-trial detention in Kazakhstan since mid-April on “inciting discord” charges, struck a plea bargain with the prosecution, under the terms of which he pled guilty, and on September 15, was released.

While Omarov avoided what could have been a long and unjustified prison sentence, he did not walk out of the courtroom a free man.

He will serve a suspended three-and-a-half-year prison sentence. He is also banned from engaging in socioeconomic and political activities for five years, which includes activities such as monitoring trials, according to his lawyer. He will not be able to resume his political satire show “Akhual Segodnya,” (The Situation Today) on YouTube, nor enjoy his fundamental right to express a social or political opinion on any online platform for the next five years. Should he violate the terms of his plea bargain he risks going to prison.

It is hard to overstate how unjust Omarov’s sentence is, even if he is not languishing in prison.

title: ‘Flock City PD:’ The Fake Flock-Owned ‘Police Department’ That Searched Real Cameras for Real People
content:
Flock created a fake police department called “Flock City PD” that it used to search a series of live automated license plate readers in several U.S. cities during demonstrations of its surveillance system’s capabilities, public records show. The records show that Flock City PD searched real cameras for people holding signs, “crowds,” people wearing masks, and more, according to audit logs shared with 404 Media. 

Flock City PD also searched extremely sensitive queries, which Flock told 404 Media were done to prove that the system would not actually perform these searches and that its moderation tools worked. title: Former Maduro Ally Pleads Guilty in US to $195M Money Laundering Scheme
content:
A Miami federal court brought a decade of investigative reporting to a close on Wednesday as Colombian-born businessman Alex Saab pleaded guilty to money laundering—years after Venezuelan news outlet Armando.info first began uncovering his state corruption schemes.

Saab, a top financial ally of ousted Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro, admitted to using the U.S. financial system to launder bribes connected to Venezuela’s Local Committees for Supply and Production (CLAP)—a state program meant to distribute food to impoverished communities. He faces up to 20 years in federal prison and has agreed to forfeit $195 million, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.

The guilty plea serves as a vindication for Armando.info, a local investigative news outlet and OCCRP member center. More than  nine years ago, the outlet pioneered reporting that brought Saab out of the shadows, exposing his ties to multimillion-dollar state contracts and the delivery of low-quality food to vulnerable populations.

At the time, Saab and the Maduro government vehemently denied the links. Saab sued the Armando.info team in Venezuela, arguing he had no connection to the CLAP program.

title: Your robotic vacuum is a witness: What home robots mean for evidence, privacy and the law
content:
A husband in Taiwan suspected his wife of having an affair. In September 2023, he found a used toothbrush at their holiday home, and garage video showed an unfamiliar man driving his wife there. Three months later, he opened their robot vacuum’s app to speak with her and saw an intimate encounter through its live camera.

He recorded the feed and used it to win about US$16,000 from his wife and her lover for infringing on his marital rights. Then the Taoyuan District Court sentenced him to five months in jail and fined him roughly $4,700 for recording private activity without consent.

Both rulings are defensible. Together, they expose a troubling gap: Devices in homes now generate evidence continuously and often invisibly, while the governing law remains a patchwork. As faculty members in a school of interdisciplinary forensics, we see such cases where forensic practice meets law that has not kept pace.

A modern robot vacuum is a mobile sensor platform. Some models combine cameras, microphones, laser navigation and remote video access, while app-connected models create detailed floor maps and cleaning histories. Their data may also reach manufacturers’ servers.

Joukko kansanedustajia eri puolueista on esittämässä, että eduskunta käsittelee kansanedustaja Timo Vornasen (tv.) jatkon tehtävässään. Asiasta kertoo STT:lle vasemmistoliiton kansanedustaja Mai Kivelä, joka on ollut asiasta yhteydessä muiden puolueiden edustajiin.

- Hän on syyllistynyt mielestäni erittäin vakaviin ja aika poikkeuksellisiin rikoksiin, joten olisi todella erikoista, jos eduskunta ei tähän millään tavalla reagoisi, Kivelä sanoo.

Vornasen ehdollisesta vankeusrangaistuksesta tuli heinäkuussa lainvoimainen. Hän ampui pistoolilla maahan helsinkiläisravintolan ulkopuolella keväällä 2024.

Kivelän mukaan tapauksen käsittelyä on hänen lisäkseen vaatimassa edustajia ainakin kokoomuksesta, SDP:stä ja vihreistä.

- Esitämme eduskunnalle, että tätä käsitellään. Sitten perustuslakivaliokunta tekee lausunnon, jonka jälkeen asiaa käsitellään täysistunnossa, Kivelä sanoo.

VASEMMISTOLIITON toisen kauden kansanedustajan mukaan kyse ei ole puoluepoliittisesta vaan eduskunnan käytäntöihin liittyvästä asiasta. Hän sanoo, ettei ole vielä muodostanut mielipidettä siihen, pitäisikö Vornasen jatkaa tehtävässään.

title: Bensalasku ei oikeastaan kasva, vaan erääntyy
content:
Markus Wasara

Donald Trump haluaa polttoaineiden hinnan alas, kun Ukraina iskee Venäjän jalostamoihin, Lähi-idän kriisi heiluttaa öljymarkkinoita ja amerikkalainen autoilija näkee seuraukset pumpulla.

Politiikasta reaktio on tuttu: näin kallista polttoaineen ei pitäisi olla. Mutta ehkä kiinnostavampi kysymys on, miksi totuimme ajattelemaan, että sen edes pitäisi olla halpaa.

Sadan vuoden ajan bensiinin ja dieselin hintaa on kutsuttu markkinahinnaksi, vaikka suuri osa niiden todellisista kustannuksista on jätetty hinnan ulkopuolelle. Totuimme ajattelemaan polttoaineen hintapiikkejä poikkeuksina. Sota syttyy, öljyreitti häiriintyy, jalostamo räjähtää tai tuottajamaa sulkee hanojaan, ja bensiinin hinta karkaa hetkeksi “normaalilta” tasoltaan.

Tässä ajattelussa on yksi ongelma: normaaliksi kutsuttu hinta ei koskaan ollut normaali markkinahinta.

Se oli hinta, josta huomattava osa laskusta puuttui.

title: Open Access in the European Research Area: progress remains uneven as new report calls for more concerted action - Research and innovation
content:
"A new independent expert report published today by the European Commission highlights that, despite notable advancement, the implementation of open access across the European Research Area remains uneven and fragmented. While progress has been made, persistent barriers continue to hinder widespread open access, and further action is needed.

Over the past decade, European Union soft-law measures, national strategies, funder mandates, and, where applicable, national legislation have advanced open access. However, these efforts have not yet produced a coherent framework across the European Research Area, leaving researchers, institutions, and funders to navigate differing policies.

The report provides a snapshot of the current open access landscape, offering policy recommendations to improve access to scientific publications and research data. It draws on an analysis of all 27 EU Member States and eight non-EU countries."

title: Culture Is the Lifeline of Our Communities, or How to Organize Events in a Country Grappling with Social Conflicts
content:
The Long Night of Museums is an initiative that began in Germany in 1997. This initiative has been held in the city of La Paz since 2007, and as of 2026, seven cities across Bolivia have joined in (El Alto, Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Tarija, Sucre, Cochabamba, as well as activities in Potosí and Beni).

The Bolivian Wikimedia team has been participating in this event for the past two years thanks to strategic coordination with the Flavio Machicado Viscarra Foundation. Through this collaboration, we have fostered the spirit of the event by organizing games, challenges, snacks, and activities that highlight Wikipedia as an open educational resource and introduce visitors to figures from both contemporary and traditional Bolivian history.

Usually, this is a night when the whole city comes alive, with a wide range of cultural activities on offer. Movie theaters, museums, bookstores, cultural venues, restaurants, and independent artists take to the streets and organize events such as fairs, concerts, and performances. It goes without saying that this day has a significant economic and social impact—cities simply feel more alive.

title: Suullinen osa yo-kokeeseen
content:
Ylioppilastutkintolautakunta on käynnistänyt vieraiden kielten ja toisen kotimaisen kielen kokeiden suullisen osan valmistelun. Suullisesta osasta on järjestetty keväällä 2026 kenttätestejä, joissa on todettu, että se on teknisesti mahdollinen toteuttaa. Vaatii kuitenkin vielä kehittämistyötä, ennen kuin suullisia tehtäviä saadaan yo-kokeisiin. Yhtenä osana tätä työtä lautakunta on järjestänyt sidosryhmätapaamisia muun muassa kieltenopettajien ainejärjestöjen kanssa alkusyksystä 2026. Kun valmistelu on pidemmällä, lautakunta pyytää lausuntoja esimerkiksi kokeiden käytännöistä ja käyttöönoton aikataulusta.

Lähtökohtana kehittämistyössä on, että kokelas voi kuunnella suullisen vastauksensa ja halutessaan äänittää sen uudestaan. Arvostelussa pääpaino on viestin välittymisessä. Ennen kuin suullinen osa tulee ylioppilaskokeisiin, kokelaat ja opettajat voivat harjoitella suullisia tehtäviä Abitti 2 -koejärjestelmässä – tämä on itse asiassa ollut mahdollista jo noin vuoden ajan. Ylioppilastutkintolautakunta laatii kokeisiin valmistautumisen tueksi myös esimerkkitehtäviä ja niin sanottuja maamerkkisuorituksia.

title: Southnord Artfest 2026: Roots En Route
content:
Roots En Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with the greenhouses – examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill the greenhouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation.

Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the insects and birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel.

Running from October 2026 through January 2027, the exhibition offers a long, unhurried encounter between art and the plant world. Set aside more time than you think you need. Walk slowly, sense carefully, and let yourself be immersed.

title: Tusen sjöars glöd – finsk glaskonst på Galleri Glas
content:
Tid: 22/10 – 13/11 2026, vernissage 21/10
Plats: Galleri Glas, Nybrogatan 34, Stockholm
Galleriets öppettider: tis–tors kl. 12–18, fre kl. 12–17, lör kl. 12–16
Fri entré.

På Galleri Glas i Stockholm öppnar utställningen Tusen sjöars glöd, som presenterar finländsk samtida glaskonst av Matias Karsikas, Harri Koskinen, Ilkka Suppanen och Renata Schirm. Utställningen har genomförts i samarbete med Finlandsinstitutet. Samtidigt visas Matias Karsikas separatutställning Nord i blom i Finlandsinstitutets galleri.

Berättelsen om Finland som glasland börjar inte med glas. Den börjar med is. Finland formgavs under istiden av det massiva istäcke som stötvis drog sig undan, plöjde upp tusentals sjöar, rullade fram rullstensåsar, forslade grus och sand i strida smältvattenströmmar, skrapade räfflor i stenhällar och slängde ut strimmor av öar i yttersta havsbandet. Sedan kom tomhet. Och därefter skogen.  Veden. Glöden. 

I denna utställning möts fyra finländska glaskonstnärer som tar glaskonsten vidare i starkt personliga uttryck. Det samtida finska konstglaset är djupt rotat i sin historia, och får här form av konstnärer som utmanar materialets gränser.

title: Tusen sjöars glöd – suomalaista lasitaidetta Galleri Glasissa
content:

Gallerian aukioloajat: ti–to klo 12–18, pe klo 12–17, la klo 12–16
Vapaa pääsy.

Tukholmalaisessa Galleri Glasissa avautuu suomalaista nykylasitaidetta esittelevä näyttely Tusen sjöars glöd. Näyttelyyn osallistuvat taiteilijat Matias Karsikas, Harri Koskinen, Ilkka Suppanen ja Renata Schirm ja se on toteutettu yhteistyössä Suomen Tukholman-instituutin kanssa. Samaan aikaan instituutin omassa galleriassa on esillä Matias Karsikkaan yksityisnäyttely Nord i blom.

Kertomus Suomesta lasitaiteestaan tunnettuna maana ei ala lasista. Se alkaa jäästä. Suomi muovautui jääkaudella valtavan mannerjään vaikutuksesta. Jääpeite vetäytyi syrjään nykäyksittäin, uurtaen maahan tuhansia järviä, muovaten harjuja, kuljettaen soraa ja hiekkaa voimakkaiden sulamisvesivirtojen mukana, raapien kalliopintoihin uurteita ja ripotellen saarivanoja ulkosaariston äärille. Sitten tuli tyhjyys. Sen jälkeen metsä. Polttopuut. Hehku.

title: AI king Jensen Huang pushes ‘responsible optimism’ at King Charles III’s gathering
content:
AYRSHIRE, Scotland — King Charles relied on all his pulling power to bring together some of the most powerful people in the world of AI to a rural corner of Scotland. 

Preparations for Thursday’s event at the 18th century estate of Dumfries House, first reported by POLITICO, had been in the works for months in close communication with the U.K. government.

But the significance of the event intensified in recent weeks after a series of alarming incidents of AI agents escaping their testing environments to hack other firms, and warnings from those in the industry that humanity’s very existence could be under threat.  

For the first time since worries about AI eradicating humanity sparked a wave of calls for immediate regulation, the companies were all under one roof. Charles addressed the dire warnings in his remarks to his guests. 

“There seems urgency in adequately considering the existential dangers of such technologies falling into the wrong hands and being used in potentially catastrophic ways,” he said. “Surely, then, we need sufficient means of control before it is all too late.”

title: Twenty-Five Political Prisoners Released, Deported from Belarus
content:
This week 25 former political prisoners arrived in Vilnius, Lithuania having been released from detention in Belarus.

Their release was negotiated by the United States special envoy to Belarus John Coale with president Aliaksander Lukashenka. In exchange, the US lifted sanctions on two Belarusian companies.

Among those released are journalist Andrei Aleksandrau and activist Iryna Zlobina, who married while in detention; lawyer Anastasiya Lazarenka, prosecuted for organizing legal consultations, among other charges; activist Alena Lazarchyk, a single parent whose communication with her child was limited by the prison management; and Sviatlana Yakubovich, a volunteer at Viasna, one of the leading human rights groups in Belarus. Most of them had been sentenced to harsh sentences of up to 14 years.

After her arrival in Vilnius, Lazarchyk told those gathered that she had not believed she would be freed until the very last moment. “One day, they say, ‘get your things.’ I was sure they were just transferring me somewhere, but they said I was being deported.”

title: University Rescinds Job Offer to Activist Who Allegedly Wiped Phone Before DHS Could Search It
content:
Georgia State University has rescinded a job offer given to a high profile activist who is currently fighting a case in which he allegedly wiped a security-focused Android phone before Customs and Border Protection (CBP) could search it. The case, which 404 Media first covered and has now received widespread and national attention, has important ramifications for privacy and when someone can still be charged with an offense even if authorities don’t have suspicion of any specific crime.

Earlier this month, activist Samuel Tunick and a group of supporters delivered a “demand letter” to the university. That letter, which Tunick shared with 404 Media, says he explained to the university he was facing a pending charge, which he describes as “an instance of textbook political repression, and a high profile civil liberties case.”

While delivering the letter, supporters held signs saying, “GSU sides with Trump,” and “Digital Privacy Under Attack!”

title: Belgian Court Rules Treasury Lacked Authority to Reject Release of Russian Assets
content:
Belgium’s supreme administrative court has ruled that a decision by the country’s treasury department refusing to release frozen Russian assets was illegal.

The court, known as the Council of State, ruled that the Administrator General of the Treasury lacked the proper legal competence to determine whether or not to release the assets.

The September 11 ruling was first reported by De Tijd on Wednesday, and shared with OCCRP. 

The case originates from a request submitted by Russia’s BCS Bank in January 2023 to unfreeze its securities and cash, which had been blocked at Brussels-based securities manager Euroclear. 

The assets were frozen following E.U. sanctions imposed in 2022 on Moscow's main securities holder, the National Settlement Depository, in response to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

In July 2024, the Belgian treasury rejected BCS Bank’s request to unfreeze its securities and cash. The treasury alleged that the lender had failed to prove it had fully severed ties with Russia’s National Settlement Depository.

The Council of State ruling does not necessarily mean the frozen funds will be released.

title: Why Hispanic Americans are losing faith in the American Dream
content:
President Donald Trump won 43% of the Hispanic vote in 2024, up from 35% in 2020 – a big gain for Republicans. Now, as the midterms approach, Hispanic Americans across party lines are losing faith in the American Dream, and his administration’s immigration crackdown appears to be part of the reason.

Arrests by Immigration and Customs Enforcement of people with no criminal record are surging. Federal immigration agents have shot at nearly two dozen people – most of them Latino – since last year, according to The New York Times. Those include the fatal shootings of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Texas and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Maine.

This climate of aggressive immigration enforcement may be affecting Hispanic Americans’ sense of belonging and their belief that they can pursue a better life in the United States. The Public Religion Research Institute 2026 survey on American identity asked more than 5,000 adults about their thoughts on the American Dream: the idea that if you work hard, you’ll get ahead. Just 40% of Hispanic Americans say that dream holds true today, down from 52% just two years ago.

title: Reframing Repositories – COAR
content:
"Scholarly communication is at a crossroads. Scholarly infrastructure has become dangerously concentrated in the hands of a small number of commercial publishers and foreign-controlled platforms, leaving institutions and nations exposed to disruptions they cannot control.

At the same time, the integrity of the scientific record is under acute strain, as AI-generated fabrications, paper mills, and reproducibility failures erode the trust on which science depends and public trust in information is fragile, at precisely the moment when citizens most need reliable access to evidence. Repositories help to address all of these challenges.

To highlight the critical importance of repositories, COAR is publishing a “Narrative Series”. The series provides several compelling, evidence-based portrayals that, taken together, build a powerful case for repositories as essential infrastructure for scholarly communications and the global knowledge commons."

title: Feeling overwhelmed by the AI doom loop? Here’s the essential reading list to make sense of it all
content:
It’s a chaotic time in an industry that’s reshaping our lives – Guardian reporters and experts recommend the books that help explain how we got here, and where we’re heading

Have you been feeling trapped in an endless cycle of artificial intelligence hype and panic? You’re not alone.

It’s a chaotic time to make sense of the industry that’s reshaping our lives, whether or not we like it. Last week, another AI company employee publicly resigned, warning the technology “could kill us all by the end of the decade”. title: First ancient DNA sample in CHARM taken!
content:
When studying medieval manuscripts, even the smallest traces of material evidence can provide valuable clues. Parchment was made from animal skins, and as it is quite well known, predominantly from calf, goat and sheepskin. However, in CHARM we are starting to find some additional species from the parchment that, to the naked eye, look exactly like the classic culprits. This is where scientific methods can help tremendously!

Now that the preliminary screening with proteomics is done for the species ID, we are starting to move further in the project to additional methods. We have now taken our very first ancient DNA sample from parchment in Riksarkivet, Stockholm. As you can see from the photograph, the sample is incredibly small, but the DNA it contains may help us to confirm and further explore the story of the animal whose skin was used to make the parchment.

This is only the beginning. The sample will now head to the laboratory in Finland, where we will find out what it can tell us. Who was this medieval animal? And what might its DNA reveal about medieval book production?

A tiny sample. One big mystery. Stay tuned!

title: European Investment Bank chief heads to Ottawa amid warming EU-Canada ties
content:
European Investment Bank President Nadia Calviño is heading to Ottawa on Sunday to lay the groundwork for Europe-Canada cooperation on critical raw materials, an official from her office said.

Calviño will be meeting with government officials including Canada’s minister for energy and natural resources, Tim Hodgson, in Ottawa.

The aim of her visit is for the European Investment Bank, the long-term lending arm of the European Union, to establish a presence in Canada and begin operations “as soon as the administrative paperwork is done, with a focus on [critical raw materials],” the official said. They were granted anonymity to speak about the internal strategy.

Coming after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday proposed admitting Canada as an associate member of the EU, Calviño’s trip is significant given that the EIB typically only operates in developing countries or members of the European Union or European Economic Area.

Ahead of this year’s G7 summit, Canada extended a behind-the-scenes offer to alliance members for “priority access” to its critical minerals stockpile, according to a letter seen by POLITICO from Hodgson.

title: Kosovo: War Crimes Verdicts are a Step Toward Justice
content:
(Berlin, September 17, 2026) – The convictions of Kosovo’s former President Hashim Thaçi and three senior former Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) leaders for war crimes on September 16, 2026, are an important step toward accountability for victims of the 1998-1999 Kosovo conflict, Human Rights Watch said today. 

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers, based in The Hague, found Thaçi, Kadri Veseli, Jakup Krasniqi, and Rexhep Selimi guilty of war crimes including murder, torture, cruel treatment, and arbitrary detention. The court acquitted the four men on charges of crimes against humanity. The convictions were for crimes committed during the war in Kosovo and northern Albania, against Kosovo Albanians, Serbs, Roma, and others. The court sentenced Thaçi and Krasniqi to 25 years, Veseli to 18 years, and Selimi to 13 years in prison.

“This verdict sends an important message to victims and their families that even powerful leaders are not beyond the reach of justice,” said Hugh Williamson, Europe and Central Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “The court’s findings underscore that accountability for serious wartime crimes should apply to everyone, regardless of their position or affiliation.”

title: Contest to Open for Ed Sheeran Flooded With Free Palestine Videos and Fart Memes
content:
After Ed Sheeran dropped Macklemore from his tour over the singer’s support for Palestine, people flooded an online contest to open for Sheeran’s Mexico City show with fart videos, bouncing WWE butts, and troll posts from usernames like “EdSheeranSupportsAndFundsGenocide.” The posts appeared live on the contest page, where people can vote for submissions they want to see win, and went up seemingly without any moderation.

Guitar Center started promoting the “Open for Legends” contest on September 14, the same day Macklemore announced he had been removed from the last 10 shows of the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s tour. Macklemore had called for a “free Palestine” on stage at his previous shows and made statements in support of Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank, Rolling Stone reported. “YOU COULD OPEN FOR ED SHEERAN,” a poster for the contest says.

The contest by Guitar Center was clearly planned before Sheeran’s tour started falling apart. Still, the timing is unfortunate. For most of Wednesday, the submissions went unmoderated and appeared on the site as they were sent.

title: Hackers Demand $3M Ransom in Revolut Data Leak
content:
A group claiming responsibility for a recent Revolut data breach has demanded 6,000 Monero—an untraceable, privacy-focused cryptocurrency—worth about $3 million, threatening to sell sensitive information belonging to hundreds of the fintech company’s customers if it is not paid within 24 hours.

The group, calling itself “iamnotavillain,” posted the ultimatum on its website on Wednesday alongside a countdown clock. It threatened to sell the information to other criminal groups if Revolut failed to pay.

A Revolut spokesperson told Reuters late Wednesday that the company had received no direct contact or ransom demand from the people claiming responsibility for the breach, and that there had been no negotiations with them.

The company first confirmed the breach on September 12, saying an unauthorized party had submitted fraudulent requests for customer information using an email account on the legitimate domain of a government agency. Revolut said its own systems and customer funds were not compromised and that it blocked the address after discovering the fraud.

title: Why AI consciousness could become the next great societal divide
content:
The debate about AI consciousness is growing, in academic articles, newspaper opinion pieces, and even among AI bots themselves. I doubt this is a passing wave of interest.

As AI systems become more capable and human-like, and more involved in our lives, the question will become harder to avoid. Many people may come to regard AI bots as conscious beings whose feelings matter. Others will strongly disagree.

I think this debate could split societies. In my chapter of the new book Perspectives on Machine Consciousness, I argue that the issue could become as divisive as abortion or climate change. Uncertainty, high stakes and competing interests are a dangerous combination.

Empirical research with my colleague Ali Ladak, currently under review, shows people are divided on this issue. When we asked 1,202 US participants whether future AI could ever become conscious, 45% considered it impossible while 23% thought it possible, with the rest unsure.

This widespread disagreement is also visible in social media posts and comments on articles. What strikes me is how confident so many people sound – whichever conclusion they are reaching.

title: Luonnonsuojeluliitto: Googlen datakeskustyömailla on mahdollisesti tehty laittomia hakkuita
content:
Teknologiajätti Googlen datakeskustyömailla on tehty epäiltyjä laittomia hakkuita. Asiasta kertoo STT:lle Suomen luonnonsuojeluliiton hallituksen puheenjohtaja Hanna Halmeenpää.

Epäilykset laittomista hakkuista kohdistuvat kahteen Googlen rakennuttamaan uuteen datakeskukseen Pohjois-Pohjanmaalla Muhoksen Leppiniemessä ja Kainuussa Kajaanin Otanmäessä. Alueilla aloitettiin jo kuukausia sitten metsätyöt, vaikka hankkeiden ympäristövaikutusten arviointi on yhä kesken.

STT on vahvistanut asian Lupa- ja valvontavirastolta (LVV), joka on aloittanut asiasta selvityksen. Otanmäen datakeskuksen osalta on vielä tarkastettava, ylittävätkö muutoshakkuiden pinta-alat YVA-rajat.

Ympäristövaikutusten arviointimenettelyä eli niin sanottua YVA-menettelyä sovelletaan hankkeisiin ja niiden muutoksiin, joilla on todennäköisesti merkittäviä ympäristövaikutuksia. Pysyvistä, yli 200 hehtaarin maakäytön muutoshakkuista tulisi lain mukaan laatia ympäristövaikutusten arviointi ennen niiden suorittamista.

Halmeenpää kuvaa tapausta törkeäksi ja Suomessa ennenkuulumattomaksi.

title: Big AI is trying to own the pathway to work. Universities shouldn’t play along | Ella Hafermalz
content:
Universities need to protect their position in education so that students have an independent pathway to employment

AI companies like OpenAI are insinuating themselves into the pathway from education to work. Soon they may claim it entirely, a disastrous result for students.

We know that students are using AI at school and at university. In conversations with those I teach, I’m struck by the trust many place in it. They turn to ChatGPT and similar tools for personal problems as well as study help. Some even doubt their abilities without AI.

Ella Hafermalz is an associate professor of work and technology at the Kin Center for Digital Innovation at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

title: Camera, lights - action!
content:
Last week, we were delighted to be invited to take part in the programme Isä, uskonto ja Marjomaa. Sampo Marjomaa from Yle visited us to explore the world of medieval texts, scribes and craftsmanship, and to find out what modern science can reveal about objects made hundreds of years ago.

For us as researchers, it was also a fun opportunity to step outside the usual research setting and in front of a camera. Being interviewed on television is quite different from presenting your research to an academic audience! Luckily, we had a wonderful team around us, and Sampo and the Yle crew made the whole experience relaxed, curious and genuinely enjoyable.

We are very grateful to Sampo and the Yle team for the invitation and for giving us the opportunity to share some of our research with an even wider audience. We are now very much looking forward to seeing the finished programme on Yle – and hopefully to introducing many more people to the fascinating world of medieval scientific detective work!

title: Sysmän rahakätköstä maailmanlaajuinen uutinen: Löydön tutkimus jatkuu
content:
Sysmästä syyskuun alussa löytynyt Suomen suurin viikinkiaikainen hopearahakätkö on saanut poikkeuksellisen laajaa kansainvälistä huomiota. Se on uutisoitu Euroopassa, Pohjois- ja Etelä-Amerikassa, Afrikassa sekä Aasiassa, ja aiheesta ovat kirjoittaneet niin valtamediat kuin arkeologiaan ja historiaan keskittyvät julkaisut. Löydöstä raportoivat muun muassa New York Times, ABC News, Good Morning America, The Times of India, Perun merkittävimpiin sanomalehtiin kuuluva La República ja Kiinan valtiollinen uutistoimisto Xinhua.

Metallinilmaisinharrastaja Kalle Lappinen löysi kätkön Sysmän kirkonkylän läheisyydestä 3. syyskuuta 2026. Löytöpaikka tarkastettiin seuraavana päivänä, ja esineet nostettiin talteen Lahden museoiden alueellisen vastuumuseon arkeologin Esko Tikkalan johdolla.

Kätkö sisältää tuhansia hopearahoja sekä maksuhopeaa, hopeisen rannerenkaan, helan ja helmen. Löydettyjen rahojen kokonaispaino on noin 4,5 kiloa. Esineet oli kätketty kahteen tuohiastiaan noin 12 metrin päähän toisistaan. Rahojen tarkka paino, määrä, alkuperä ja ajoitus selviävät jatkotutkimuksissa.

title: Jensen Huang: Don’t regulate AI like social media
content:
AYRSHIRE, SCOTLAND — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said AI should not be regulated like social media because AI is a “technology” rather than a “product.”

Speaking at an AI event convened by King Charles III at Dumfries House in Ayrshire, Scotland, Huang told journalists that AI is “very different than social media” and that at present the security issues involving AI are “related to products not ready to be released.”

His remarks come as governments around the world are grappling with whether to place regulatory constraints on AI, and after AI executives, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, have called for a slowing of AI development.

“Unlike social media, which is a product, AI is a technology that’s behind all of these other tech, all of these products — and so, regulate the products,” Huang said.

He said authorities should monitor for when an AI deployment “goes wrong” and “whenever new laws are necessary, add to the existing laws,” but pointed out that there are existing regulations in sectors where AI is deployed such healthcare, transportation, and entertainment.

title: Amin Shirafkan and Alireza Hajatmand Arrested in Gorgan
content:
According to HRANA, Amin (Mazdak) Shirafkan and Alireza Hajatmand were arrested in Gorgan.

An informed source close to the families of the two individuals confirmed the news to HRANA and said: “On Wednesday, September 16, officers from the Public Security and Intelligence Police went to Mr. Shirafkan’s workplace, located in the Shirangi Passage in Gorgan, and arrested him along with his shop assistant, identified as Alireza Hajatmand. They were subsequently transferred to a detention facility operated by the Criminal Investigation Police.”

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for their arrests or the charges brought against them.

Amin Shirafkan is 48 years old, while Alireza Hajatmand is 20 and is from the city of Aq Qala. Of the two, Amin (Mazdak) Shirafkan has previously been arrested and received judicial convictions in connection with his activities.

title: I Hijacked a Real Artist's Spotify with AI Music. It Was Disturbingly Easy
content:
On September 10, the Brooklyn-based punk band Lathe of Heaven released a new single on its verified Spotify page called Riding High. Any fan of Lathe of Heaven would have immediately noticed that the song sounded nothing like the band’s previous work, that the vocals were not from lead singer Gage Allison, and that the album cover was widely different from the style and logo the band used previously. 

That’s because Lathe of Heaven didn’t write, perform, or willingly release Riding High. I created the song with a simple prompt given to the AI music generator Udio, and I was able to release the track on Lathe of Heaven’s official Spotify page, as well as on its Apple Music, Tidal, and Amazon Music pages, without the band’s knowledge, by exploiting a glaring loophole in the way music is digitally distributed to streaming platforms.

title: Israeli Firm May Have Run Angola Influence Campaign
content:
Israeli influence-for-hire company BlackCore appears to have trained members of an Angolan government communications team and helped them run a covert social media campaign, according to research by the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab.

Citizen Lab examined websites and other online infrastructure linked to BlackCore and obtained what researchers identified as the company’s final report on a training program in Angola. One BlackCore webpage, titled “Angolan Government Campaign,” advertised training in storytelling, copywriting, traffic management and social media operations. It also described plans to launch live campaigns on Meta and TikTok.

The final report said the program began on January 19, 2026, and continued for more than 14 weeks, ending sometime in April. BlackCore described the goal as replacing what it called “amateur production practices” with a “professional, robust, and scalable Architecture for State communications.”

According to the report, participants produced more than 40 pieces of content, while trainers evaluated at least 24 publications. Materials reviewed by Citizen Lab also showed Facebook and Instagram accounts and pages used in the campaign.

title: Nyt se on varmaa: punavihreä blokki nappasi voiton Ruotsin vaaleissa – Kristersson on jättänyt eroanomuksen
content:
Ruotsin äärimmäisen täpärät valtiopäivävaalit kääntyvät vasemman blokin voitoksi.

Punavihreä-keskustalainen opposition blokki on saamassa valtiopäiville 176 edustajaa ja oikeiston blokki 173, kertovat vaaliviranomaiset.

Suurin puolue on odotetusti sosiaalidemokraatit 28 prosentin ääniosuudella ja 99 valtiopäiväedustajalla. Maltillinen kokoomus on kerännyt 19,8 prosentin kannatuksen ja saa 70 edustajaa ja ruotsidemokraatit 17,5 prosentin kannatuksen ja 62 edustajaa.

Sosiaalidemokraattien puheenjohtajan Magdalena Anderssonin odotetaan käynnistävän neuvottelut hallituksen muodostamiseksi, kertoo uutistoimisto TT.

RUOTSIN pääministeri Ulf Kristersson on jättänyt eroanomuksen tehtävästään.

Kristersson kertoo asiasta viestipalvelu X:ssä, jossa hän on julkaissut kuvan valtiopäivien puhemiehelle Andreas Norlénille osoitetusta kirjeestä.

Hän pyytää vapautusta pääministerin tehtävästä, jotta uuden hallituksen muodostaminen voidaan aloittaa välittömästi.

title: SoKiD 2.0: Bringing the Kadazandusun Language into the Digital World through Wiktionary
content:
What if a word we add today becomes part of the digital heritage of the Kadazandusun language for generations to come?

On 9th September 2026, 70 students from 15 primary schools across Sabah gathered at Sekolah Kebangsaan Tengkurus in Kota Belud with a purpose that may seem simple, but carries great significance: to document Kadazandusun vocabulary in the digital world through Wiktionary.

This was SoKiD 2.0, short for Sompuruan Komi Boros Kadazandusun, or Kadazandusun Vocabulary Group.

Kadazandusun is one of the major languages spoken by communities in Sabah. However, like many heritage languages, its use among younger generations faces various challenges.

In schools, students may still have a limited command of basic vocabulary. Some may recognise a word but have difficulty understanding its meaning, context, or how to use it in a sentence. When vocabulary is limited, learning, writing, and communicating in one’s mother tongue can also become more challenging.

This is where SoKiD takes a different approach.

Rather than simply memorising words, students are encouraged to identify, understand, edit, and document Kadazandusun vocabulary themselves in the digital world through Wiktionary.

title: Spilling the Truth: Rethinking River Lea’s Storm Overflow Crisis Maps
content:
by Jakleen Al-Dalal’a and Artemis Skarlatidou

When a combined sewer overflow releases sewage into a river, how do people actually find out, and do they trust what they are being told? 

On 18 July 2026, residents, river users, and representatives from local organisations and community groups met at UCL East to work through that question together. The session is part of CHRYSES Project, a European research collaboration examining how environmental health crises are understood, remembered and communicated. It forms part of a growing series of workshops and events exploring these questions across different rivers and communities and following on from an earlier session in which participants mapped what crisis along the River Lea actually looks and feels like, drawing on memory, routine and everyday use of the river rather than official and formal data. Across both sessions, a consistent concern has been how lived experience and public data meet – or fail to meet – when people try to understand what is happening to the rivers they care about.

title: COST Actions at the 9th World One Health Congress
content:
The 9th World One Health Congress (WOHC2026) brought together researchers, policymakers and experts from around the world to explore the interconnected health of people, animals and the environment. Seven COST Actions showcased their work and brought their research networks into discussions on some of today’s most pressing One Health challenges.

The importance of the One Health approach has grown significantly in recent years as health challenges increasingly cross the boundaries between humans, animals and the environment. Antimicrobial resistance, emerging infectious diseases, climate change and other complex challenges demonstrate how closely these areas are interconnected and how difficult it can be to address them in isolation. Tackling these issues therefore requires international collaboration across disciplines and sectors, as well as the exchange of knowledge and expertise between different research communities.

title: Etla ennustaa: kasvukäänne vahvistuu ja investointihanat aukeavat
content:
Talouskasvu vahvistuu tänä vuonna 1,7 prosenttiin ja nousee ensi vuonna jo lähelle kahta prosenttia, arvioi Elinkeinoelämän tutkimuslaitos. Etlan ennusteen mukaan Suomi pysyttelee lähivuosina kasvussa kiinni. Erityisesti investoinnit tuottavat kasvusysäyksen ja lisääntyvät tänä vuonna yli viisi prosenttia ja ensi vuonna reilut 9 prosenttia. Ensi vuoden investointien kasvu tulee suurelta osin hakukoneyhtiö Googlen ilmoittamista datakeskusinvestoinneista. Yksityinen kulutus kasvaa tänä vuonna ja kasvukäänne alkaa vihdoin vuoden lopulla näkyä myös työmarkkinoilla, joskin sitä ennen työttömyysaste ehtii kivuta ennätyksellisen korkealle.

  • Talouskasvu vahvistuu 1,7 prosenttiin tänä vuonna viennin, investointien ja yksityisen kulutuksen vetämänä. Ensi vuodelle Etla ennustaa 1,9 prosentin kasvua ja vuonna 2028 bkt:n ennustetaan kasvavan 1,4 prosenttia.
  • Tavaravienti yltää uusiin ennätyksiin. Suomen viennin kasvuksi arvioidaan 3,7 prosenttia tänä vuonna ja kolme prosenttia ensi vuonna.

title: Kansallisarkiston ja tutkimusyhteisön strateginen yhteistyöryhmä aloittaa toimintansa
content:
Kansallisarkisto on asettanut Kansallisarkiston ja tutkimusyhteisön strategisen yhteistyöryhmän.

Ryhmän tavoitteena on vahvistaa pidemmän aikavälin vuoropuhelua tutkimusyhteisön ja Kansallisarkiston välillä sekä auttaa ennakoimaan eri tieteenalojen muuttuvia tutkimustarpeita.

Yhteistyöryhmässä on edustettuna laajalti eri tieteenaloja – historiantutkimusta, yhteiskuntatieteitä ja luonnontieteitä – sekä korkeakoulujen johtoa ja julkisen hallinnon yhteistyötahoja.

“Kansallisarkisto kehittää tulevina vuosina arkistoaineistojen tutkimuskäytön kansallista digitaalista infrastruktuuria, ja yhteistyöryhmässä edustettu asiantuntemus auttaa meitä työn strategisessa suuntaamisessa”, tutkimuspäällikkö Miikka Voutilainen kertoo.

Ryhmän toimikausi on 15.9.2026–31.12.2030, ja ryhmä kokoustaa noin kolme kertaa vuodessa.

Kansallisarkisto on merkittävällä tavalla uudistamassa palveluitaan. Muutoksen taustalla ovat asiakaskäyttäytymisen muutos, toimintamenomäärärahojen huomattava väheneminen sekä digitalisaation nopea kehitys.

Kansallisarkiston strategisena tavoitteena on palvella eri tieteenalojen tutkimusta ja kehittää digitaalisia palveluja vastaamaan tutkimuksen muuttuviin tarpeisiin.
