title: Conference greetings: ESA conference 2026
content:
This year’s European Sociology Association conference was held in Warsaw, Poland on 25-28 August. CEACG’s researchers Mark Tarplee, Michael Egerer, Veera Kankainen, and Sébastien Berret took part in the conference and contributed with their presentations. 

The conference brought together over 3000 sociologists from all over the world, and provided almost an unlimited selection of topics and presentations to choose from: 

“All in all, it was great to see so many sociologists presenting, and so many topics explored. Nevertheless, due to the sheer size of the conference, it was only possible to visit four sessions per day. There were many occasions in which I was unable to attend sessions because I had committed to another one”, says Mark. 

“Another thing that I was surprised about was how much we live in our own sociological bubbles. The diversity and scope of the programme was a reminder that Sociology is indeed very fragmented. The conference offered a welcome opportunity to challenge one’s usual notions and get fresh ideas”, Michael adds.

title: CAE’s reactions to SOTEU 2026
content:
Today’s State of the Union left us at Culture Action Europe with mixed feelings.  

On the one hand, from a cultural perspective, there was a lot we could recognise ourselves in: fighting together for our European idea, standing up for values, protecting Europe’s unique social model, and affirming that ‘in Europe, people will always come first.’  

 Culture runs through all of this. It is inseparable from Ukraine’s struggle to preserve its identity. From how we challenge narratives that divide us. From how children encounter the world and learn to use imagination. The proposed Congress of Europe feels like an obvious space for artists and cultural organisations to help shape a new vision for Europe.  

 On the other hand, concrete commitments to support the cultural sector were absent. Today marks 1099 days since cultural diversity was last mentioned in a 2023 SOTEU address. 

Today, a lot was said about AI and ‘the highest-quality data,’ which is ‘a precious European treasure,’ while ignoring that much of this data is sourced without asking or paying the authors and creators behind it.

title: Amos Rexin uusi ryhmänäyttely avaa afrikkalaisia ja afropohjoismaisia näkökulmia maailmasta
content: Voisiko olla olemassa toisenlaisia tapoja ymmärtää maailmaa? Tätä kysymystä tarkastellaan Amos Rexin syysnäyttelyssä Vuoren toisella puolen – Merkintöjä afrikkalaisista ja afropohjoismaisista näkökulmista (The Other Side of the Mountain). Näyttely kokoaa yhteen yksitoista sekä Afrikan mantereella että afropohjoismaisessa diasporassa työskentelevää nykytaiteilijaa. Heidän teoksensa osoittavat, miten erilaiset tavat tietää, kokea ja tarkastella ympäristöjämme voivat laajentaa käsitystämme todellisuudesta. Näyttely jatkaa Amos Rexin pitkäjänteistä työtä tuomalla maailmanluokan nykytaidetta pohjoismaisen yleisön ulottuville ja luomalla kohtaamisia kansainvälisten taidekäytäntöjen ja pohjoismaisten näkökulmien välille.

title: Moderni klassikko Amadeus ensi-iltaan Rovaniemen Teatterissa
content:
Rovaniemen Teatteri avaa Tieva-näyttämön syksyn modernilla klassikolla Amadeus. Peter Shafferin käsikirjoitus on fiktiivinen tarina historiallisten henkilöiden 1780-luvun ajan jatkuneesta kilvoittelusta ja halusta luoda toinen toistaan ikiaikaisempia sävellyksiä.

Rovaniemen Teatterissa nähtävä Amadeus on karnevalistinen ja intohimoinen kertomus musiikista, neroudesta ja keskinkertaisuuden kirouksesta. Se paljastaa, miten ihailu, kateus ja viha kietoutuvat toisiinsa – ja kuinka pitkälle ihminen on valmis menemään joutuessaan nöyryytetyksi. Se näyttää, miten vallanpitäjien mielistely ja juonittelu voivat murentaa lokaan kaikkein ylevimmätkin pyrkimykset.

Suurella Tieva-näyttämöllä koetaan näyttävä kokonaisuus, jossa on puheteatterin ja pukuloiston lisäksi sirkustaidetta, akrobatiaa, live-musiikkia ja oopperaa. Ensi-iltaa vietetään lauantaina 19.9.2026.

Teoksen ohjaa Maiju Sallas, lavastuksesta vastaa Annukka Pykäläinen, koreografia on Antton Laineen käsialaa, nelihenkistä orkesteria johtaa Lapin Kamariorkesterin Anna Laakso ja pukusuunnittelusta vastaa Paula Varis. Salierina katkeroituu Marko Syysmaa ja Mozartina lapsekasta elämäniloa pursuaa Timo Vuento.

title: Webinaari: Traumainformoitu lähestymistapa museossa 24.11.2026
content:
Webinaari: Traumainformoitu lähestymistapa museossa
Paikka: Zoom Webinars
Aika: Tiistai 24.11.2026 klo 13–16 (UTC+2)
Kieli: Suomi ja englanti
Osallistuminen: ilmainen, ennakkoilmoittautuminen

Traumainformoitu lähestymistapa museossa -webinaari tarjoaa katsauksen siihen, mitä traumainformoitu työote tarkoittaa ja miten sitä voidaan soveltaa museokontekstissa. Ohjelmassa kuullaan asiantuntijoiden, kokemusasiantuntijoiden sekä museo- ja järjestökentän edustajien puheenvuoroja, jotka avaavat lähestymistavan keskeisiä periaatteita sekä käytännön esimerkkejä museotyössä, mielenterveystyössä ja vapaaehtoistoiminnassa. Lisäksi tarkastellaan traumainformoidun työotteen merkitystä museopedagogiikassa sekä yleisö- ja yhteisötyössä. Osallistujat pääsevät työstämään pohdintatehtävää webinaarin teemoista, ja tehtävien koonnit jaetaan kaikille osallistujille webinaarin jälkeen. Webinaarin tavoitteena on vahvistaa ymmärrystä turvallisempien, saavutettavien ja erilaisia kokemuksia huomioivien museoympäristöjen rakentamisesta sekä tarjota käytännöllisiä työkaluja oman työn kehittämiseen.

Miten pitkälle pääsimme kumppanikirjastojen ja yhteistyökumppaneiden kanssa, kun vuonna 2025 aloitimme kirjaston lukuaskeleiden ottamisen?

Kirjaston lukuaskeleen  OPH:n rahoittama osuus päättyy vuoden 2026 lopussa. Järjestämme hankkeen päätteeksi ja tulosten esittelemiseksi webinaarin torstaina 12.11. klo 12–16.

title: Forskningens frihet har försvagats i Finland – riksdagsvalet avgör riktningen
content:
Tillsammans med flera andra vetenskapliga organisationer uppmanar vi partier och kandidater att berätta hur de tänker trygga förutsättningarna för fri forskning.

Finland har tappat mark som ett av de ledande länderna när det gäller forskningsfrihet. Forskare utsätts i allt högre grad för trakasserier, och deras arbete påverkas allt mer av politisk och ekonomisk styrning. Samtidigt ökar behovet av oberoende, forskningsbaserad kunskap till följd av miljökriser och andra säkerhetshot, ekonomisk oro och desinformation.

I riksdagsvalet våren 2027 väljer vi de beslutsfattare som avgör förutsättningarna för forskning och ny kunskap i Finland. Väljarna har rätt att kräva tydliga svar av kandidaterna: Hur tänker de försvara forskningens och forskarnas frihet? Hur ska forskningens långsiktiga finansiering tryggas? Och hur tänker de stärka den öppna vetenskapens ställning och användningen av forskningsbaserad kunskap i beslutsfattandet?

En grupp centrala aktörer inom vetenskapsområdet lyfter fram dessa frågor i valdebatten genom kampanjen Släpp forskningen fri.

title: New senior advisor joins the support team
content:
After 14 years abroad, Jenni is back in Helsinki. She has previously worked for Music Finland, the British Council, and the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA), one of the world’s leading documentary film festivals and a documentary film institute. For the past three years, while working as Head of New Media Operations at IDFA, she led the activities of the interdisciplinary platform IDFA Doc-Lab, which brings together documentary storytelling, technology, and art. Throughout her career, Jenni has worked on everything from network-building in the cultural sector and funding advice to mapping industry needs and measuring programme impact. Jenni holds a master’s degree in film exhibition and curation and a bachelor’s degree in journalism and communication.

A very warm welcome, Jenni!

title: Naturvetenskap, samhällsstyre och folkhälsa – så ska 232 internationella studenter göra skillnad
content:
För att få stipendiet krävs, utöver akademiska meriter, arbetslivserfarenhet, ledarskapserfarenhet och potential att bidra till samhällsutveckling. Årets 232 stipendiater ska studera vid 28 svenska universitet inom bland annat teknik, naturvetenskap, innovation, entreprenörskap, folkhälsa och samhällsstyre.

Uppföljningar av tidigare stipendiater visar att kunskaper och erfarenheter från tiden i Sverige används även efter avslutade studier:

  • 94 procent använder kunskaper och färdigheter från studierna i sitt arbete.
  • 90 procent arbetar i roller som bidrar till hållbar utveckling.
  • 30 procent har professionellt samarbete eller utbyte med Sverige efter studierna.

    • För många tidigare stipendiater har tiden i Sverige också blivit början på långvariga relationer med svenska universitet, organisationer och yrkesnätverk.

    Ett exempel är Noore Wazid Lamin från Bangladesh, som studerade tillämpad miljövetenskap vid Halmstad universitet med stipendium från SI. I dag arbetar han med vatten, sanitet och hållbarhet i Bangladesh. Sedan studierna har han bland annat utbildat över 400 personer och bidragit till att bygga 68 system för insamling av regnvatten.

title: From the Autistici/Inventati Case to a European Dispute over Financial Autonomy
content:
We have drafted a proposal: can the European Commission protect Autistici/Inventati from the effects of the sanctions imposed by the Trump administration? We have spoken with lawyers, involved several Members of Parliament, and we know that there is a legal avenue to protect European citizens, organisations and banks from the extraterritorial effects of these sanctions. But legal instruments need to be matched by the political force required to use them.

Banca Etica, by contrast, continues to argue that fighting to make this happen is not its responsibility and that its priority is simply to protect itself. Ilaria Salis and Benedetta Scuderi are already taking action in the European Parliament, but the road will be long. I firmly believe that this is not the time to remain indifferent.

In a September in which far-right forces continue to advance in Germany, and in which the United States is placing people and organisations committed to antifascism and the defence of rights on a blacklist, despite there being no judicial conviction against them in Italy or the European Union, the response cannot be: let it go, better not to raise our heads too much.

title: The Genius Logic of the NATO Phonetic Alphabet: How It Was Created & How It Works
content: Most of us can rattle off the first few words-that-stand-for-letters of the NATO phonetic alphabet. Alfa, Bravo, and Charlie no doubt come right to mind, and depending on how many war movies you’ve seen, so may Delta, Echo, and Foxtrot. But how many of us would recognize Kilo, Mike, and Sierra? For that matter, how much do any of us know about how these particular words came to be used to spell out other words when communicating over walkie-talkies or other low-fidelity communication systems? In the video above for his YouTube channel RobWords, YouTuber Rob Watts explains the development of and logic behind the NATO phonetic alphabet, wasting no time in clarifying that it isn’t a phonetic alphabet, nor was it created by NATO.

title: A “High Octane” Kate McKinnon at the National Book Festival
content:
-This is a guest post by Sahar Kazmi, a public affairs specialist in the Office of the Chief Information Officer.

“I’m so shy!” Kate McKinnon belted out just moments after dancing across the ballroom stage at the National Book Festival, delighting the huge crowd that turned out for her appearance on the Main Stage.

In conversation with broadcast journalist Amna Nawaz, McKinnon — a New York Times bestselling author and Emmy-winning comedian who starred on Saturday Night Live for a decade — said that even though she loves people and performance, she is actually “the most introvert you could possibly be.”

Her jovial, joke-filled interview, along with a Q&A that saw McKinnon bounding from one end of the stage to the other (and even hopping into the crowd to get a closer listen to one attendee’s question), offered no doubt that the author can turn on her social battery when she needs to. McKinnon was at this year’s festival to discuss her popular middle-grade book series about the eccentric scientist Millicent Quibb and her three young protégés, the Porch sisters.


(The full video of McKinnon’s appearance at the National Book Festival is at the link above. Her segment begins at 1:52:00.)

title: California Is Being Asked to Give Up 14 Years of Broadband Protections. It Doesn't Have To.
content:
Accepting $1.42 billion in federal broadband funding would require California to give up enforcing its net neutrality, affordability, and public-safety laws against its biggest providers. The state can get the money without the catch — by challenging the condition in court first.

In the summer of 2018, California learned what happens when no one can hold internet providers accountable.

As the Mendocino Complex Fire, then the largest wildfire in California history, tore across the north of the state, Santa Clara County firefighters were called in to help. They relied on a mobile internet connection to coordinate the thousands of personnel and vehicles racing to contain the fire. In the middle of that emergency, Verizon throttled their connection down to an unusable trickle. Despite the firefighters' pleas, Verizon refused to restore full service unless they upgraded to a more expensive plan, forcing crews to fall back on personal phones to keep their systems running during a disaster.

title: Extending the Digital Fairness Act to the knowledge economy
content:
With the Digital Fairness Act (DFA) the Commission aims to address a number of pressing issues faced by consumers and businesses in the digital environment. This includes dark patterns, addictive design, unfair personalisation and pricing practices as well as unfair digital contracts.

In the digital environment, consumers often face situations that are not designed to be in their best interest, but rather to extract their money or time. As a result, the discussions around the DFA are already shaping up to focus on a few hot topics such as dark patterns, addictive design and protection of minors. However, the DFA also presents a great opportunity to strengthen access to knowledge and culture in Europe, and to remedy some of the failings of the digital licensing market.

title: Victory! Appeals Court Rejects Expansive New Copyright Claim
content:
The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit handed internet users and programmers a big win today, by rejecting an attempt to stretch a narrow provision of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) into a new source of copyright liability.  

The case involves Section 1202 of the DMCA, which prohibits intentionally removing copyright management information (CMI) like an author’s name or a copyright notice, from a copyrighted work. Open AI and Microsoft used code from Github as part of the training data for their LLMs, along with billions of other works. A group of anonymous Github contributors sued, alleging the new code coming out of these LLMs was similar to theirs—but with the CMI stripped out.  

The Ninth Circuit correctly agreed with what we said in our brief: removing copyright information from a copyrighted work is fundamentally different from creating a new work that didn't have CMI in the first place. Section 1202 of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act was intended to serve as a backstop for traditional copyrights in the digital age—not to create a new, more expansive right to inhibit otherwise non-infringing uses.

title: What AI urgency? Industry and leaders split on how to handle advanced tech’s threats
content:
The seeming unanimity among artificial intelligence industry powerhouses about addressing AI’s potential threats to humanity is already splintering.

Four days after OpenAI, Anthropic and Elon Musk locked arms behind a call to slow AI’s advances, a phalanx of industry leaders and lawmakers speaking Wednesday at POLITICO’s Decoded Summit came to no consensus on how to regulate the technology — despite mostly agreeing that it’s a task someone should lead.

Anthropic policy chief Sarah Heck declined to endorse the same proposal for congressionally mandated independent AI monitoring that OpenAI had backed the day before. Progressive Rep. Greg Casar (D-Texas) advocated mandatory limits on the technology and the creation of a federal agency to regulate it, while House Energy and Commerce Chair Brett Guthrie (R-Ky.) said speed is less important than getting the policy right — and the two clashed on whether Americans should care about beating China.

title: Kosovo: War crimes convictions of former president ‘shows senior officials are not above the law’
content:
Reacting to the convictions for war crimes of Hashim Thaçi, Kadri Veseli, Rexhep Selimi and Jakup Krasniqi by the Kosovo Specialist Chamber, Esther Major, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for Europe, said: 

These verdicts give hope that the victims and relatives of the missing will finally see justice

Esther Major, Amnesty International

These verdicts give hope that the victims and relatives of the missing will finally see justice

“These convictions give hope to thousands of victims of the Kosovo war who have waited for more than two decades to get justice for the horrific crimes committed against them and to know the fate of their loved ones.  

“These convictions show that senior officials are not above the law. 

“These verdicts give hope that any attempt to obstruct justice, truth and reparation will not be tolerated, and that the victims and relatives of the missing will finally see justice.” 

Background

The Trial Panel of the Kosovo Specialist Chamber found the four former officials guilty of the war crimes of arbitrary detention against 385 individuals, cruel treatment against 49 individuals, torture against 303 individuals, and murder against 96 individuals.

title: Report on the Latest Status of Detained Sunni Citizens in Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, 10 Sunni citizens in Ahvaz, including Majid Sharifi (Savari), Arkan Sharifi (Savari), 17, Razi Heydari, Hossein Heydari, Abdolhadi Asakereh, Lafteh Heydari, Hamzeh Sayahi, and Mohammad Savari, remain in detention.

According to information received by HRANA, Majid Sharifi (Savari), 44, remains held at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility in Ahvaz. The other seven identified detainees have been transferred to the quarantine ward of Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz. Majid Sharifi suffers from kidney failure, and reports received by HRANA indicate that he is in poor physical condition. Given his underlying medical condition, his continued detention at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility has raised concerns among his relatives about his health.

These citizens were arrested on September 4, 2026, by Ministry of Intelligence agents at Majid Sharifi’s home in the Kuy-e Mashali neighborhood of Ahvaz. The arrests were carried out without the presentation of a judicial warrant and were accompanied by physical violence.

title: China: New Border Decree Curtails Right to Leave
content:
(New York) – A new Chinese government decree expands the discretion of administrative authorities to arbitrarily bar people from leaving China, violating the internationally protected right to leave a country, Human Rights Watch said today. The State Council’s 19-article Regulations on Exit-Entry Administration, known as Decree No. 841, took effect on September 15, 2026.

The new decree restricts nationals and non-nationals from leaving China for a range of ill-defined reasons of national security and risk. However, under international human rights law, any legal restrictions on leaving a country must be necessary and proportionate for legitimate aims.

“The Chinese government is tightening its rules to decide arbitrarily who can and cannot leave China, violating the internationally protected right to leave one’s country,” said Maya Wang, deputy Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “The authorities have increasingly subjected human rights defenders and ethnic minorities to restrictions and scrutiny of their international travel, but everyone including foreigners should worry about their ability to leave China.”

title: Reading The Tealeaves in Hong Kong
content:
By Jonathan Power

LUND, Sweden | 16 September 2026 (IDN) — In 1995, in a little-remembered event, Li Ruthuan, a member of the Chinese Politburo (containing the top seven in the government), made a speech likening the Chinese takeover of Hong Kong to the case of a lady who had agreed to sell a 100-year-old Yi-Xiang teapot that was famous for the taste of the tea it poured. Unbeknown to her, its quality derived from the residue that had accumulated on the inside of the pot. Eager to prepare the pot for sale, she cleaned and polished it. When the purchaser tried using the pot, the tea was dreadful, and he demanded his money back.

title: Africa is bigger than we’ve been led to believe – what next?
content:
A new map of the world rescales the size of Africa and calls into question our perception of land, power and influence

This month, the UN passed a resolution, brought to the assembly by Togo, to phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe and replace it with another that shows the real scale of territories. That’s right – when it comes to size, the map of the world we have all grown up with is not accurate. The main loser of land on the Mercator map is Africa, and the new “Equal Earth” map reflects its true proportions. I spoke to our west Africa correspondent Eromo Egbejule about his extensive reporting on the map changes, and why people feel so strongly about it.

Seeing the new map transposed over the old might make you feel oddly disoriented. Logically, there is absolutely no immediate tangible impact on one’s life that comes out of knowing that the entire top part of the northern hemisphere is so much smaller than you were led to believe. And yet, there is still something agitating about it, like you’ve been the subject of a lifelong trick, or at least a breach of trust.

title: “A Recurring Pattern”: Civilians Paying the Price in Mali’s Drone Campaign
content:
Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published.

WARNING: This report contains links to graphic images and footage.

A joint Bellingcat and Jeune Afrique investigation into drone strikes carried out by the Malian military adds new details about the attacks which frequently are carried out in civilian areas and have reportedly resulted in the deaths of civilians.

The incidents, concentrated in northern Mali, often involved strikes on vehicles or commercial activity. Video footage of the strikes is often broadcast on national television, portrayed as precise attacks against terrorists and their logistics. 

Mali’s military government acquired its first Turkish-made Bayraktar TB2 drones in late 2022, and regularly releases footage of drone strikes to be broadcast on national television, describing them as “precise” and describing the targets as “terrorists and their logistics”. This month marks three years since Mali joined with Burkina Faso and Niger to form the Alliance of Sahel States (AES). Its military government has made restoring national sovereignty a central part of its political message.

title: Thousands Protest in Malta After Businessman Acquitted in Journalist's Murder
content:
Outrage spilled onto the streets of the Maltese capital on Wednesday evening as demonstrators gathered at the heart of Valletta, shifting from vigils to protests to demand political accountability following the acquittal of the alleged mastermind behind the 2017 assassination of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia.

For 107 consecutive months - on the 16th of every month since Caruana Galizia was killed by a car bomb outside her home - civil society groups held silent vigils. But the Sept. 2 acquittal of Yorgen Fenech, a prominent businessman accused of orchestrating and financing the plot, transformed that quiet grief into open defiance.

Chanting “Mafia! Mafia!” and “Injustice!”, thousands of protesters marched from the Parliament building to a memorial standing directly opposite Malta’s Law Courts to lay flowers and light candles before Caruana Galizia’s portrait. Banners carried by the crowd called for the protection of journalists and democracy, declaring: “The Trial Has Ended. Our Work Has Not” and “Impunity Ends Here.”

title: What to Know About Mail-In Voting for the 2026 Midterms
content:
This week, the Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s plans to impose new rules for mail-in voting for the midterm elections in November. 

In a March executive order, President Donald Trump had instructed the U.S. Postal Service to create rules for election officials sending mail-in ballots to voters. If a state didn’t comply with the new rules, the Postal Service wouldn’t deliver the ballots to voters. State officials said it would have been impossible to comply in time, and two federal judges blocked the rule for the November elections. Lawyers for the Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to intervene.

In a brief, unsigned order on Monday, the court’s majority denied the administration’s request, writing that the “Government is unlikely to succeed on the merits of its challenge.” Justice Samuel Alito wrote an eight-page dissent, joined by Justice Clarence Thomas, saying he would have allowed the rules to go into effect. The court has not yet decided whether the rules can move forward after the November election.

Trump criticized the Supreme Court’s order in a Truth Social post on Tuesday, calling it “a big loss for Republicans, and America itself.”

title: Kaavoituksen sujuvoittaminen ei saa tapahtua osallisuuden ja ympäristön laadun kustannuksella
content:
Hallituksen esitys alueidenkäyttölaiksi on edennyt valiokuntakäsittelyyn. Esityksessä tavoitellaan kaavoituksen sujuvoittamista.

Vaikka sujuva kaavoitus on kannatettava tavoite, sitä ei tule toteuttaa kansalaisten osallistumis- ja vaikutusmahdollisuuksia heikentämällä. Kuntalaisten näkemykset ovat keskeinen osa kaavoitusta asiantuntijatiedon rinnalla.

Ehdotetut muutokset tekevät kuntalaisten osallistumisesta nykyistä haastavampaa, vaikka kaavoitusjärjestelmä pysyisi lakiehdotuksen mukaan pääosin ennallaan. Kaavoitusta on seurattava aktiivisesti, digitaalisessa ympäristössä on osattava toimia ja ottaa kantaa oikeaan aikaan.

Kansalaisten valitusoikeus on keskeinen osa alueidenkäytön järjestelmää ja demokraattista päätöksentekoa. Perustuslain 20 § velvoittaa julkisen vallan turvaamaan jokaiselle mahdollisuuden vaikuttaa elinympäristöään koskevaan päätöksentekoon.

Nykyisessä lainsäädännössä valitusoikeus on kunnan jäsenillä sekä asianosaisilla. Lakiehdotus rajaisi valitusoikeuden asemakaavasta niihin, joiden oikeuteen, velvollisuuteen tai etuun päätös välittömästi vaikuttaa.

title: Nordic Digital Music Survey 2026: Vaikka tekoälyn yleinen käyttö on kasvanut, vaativat pohjoismaalaiset musiikilta läpinäkyvyyttä ja ihmisen luovuutta
content:
Tekoälystä on tullut nopeasti osa pohjoismaalaisten arkea, mutta suhtautuminen tekoälyn tuottamaan musiikkiin on muuttunut aiempaa kriittisemmäksi. Tämä selviää Pohjoismaiden musiikin tekijöiden tekijänoikeusjärjestöjen Teoston, Kodan (Tanska) ja TONOn (Norja) tuoreesta Nordic Digital Music Survey 2026 -tutkimuksesta.

Tuoreen tutkimuksen mukaan tekoälyä omassa arjessaan tai työssään käyttävien ruotsalaisten, suomalaisten, norjalaisten ja tanskalaisen osuus on kasvanut ainoastaan kahdessa vuodessa 20 prosentista 66 prosenttiin. Samaan aikaan asenteet tekoälymusiikkia vastaan ovat selvästi tiukentuneet.

Suurin osa, lähes 80 prosenttia pohjoismaalaisista katsoo, että ilman ihmisen luovaa panosta tuotettu tekoälymusiikki pitäisi merkitä selkeästi kanavissa, joissa niitä on tarjolla. Vuonna 2024 merkintää kannatti vain 58 prosenttia vastaajista. Suomessa suhtautuminen tekoälymusiikkiin on Pohjoismaiden kriittisintä, sillä peräti 81 prosenttia suomalaisista on sitä mieltä, että ilman ihmisen luovaa panosta tuotettu tekoälymusiikki pitäisi merkitä selkeästi.

title: Women, Innovation and Impact: Illustrating the global progress of WIPO’s first IP and Gender Action Plan
content: The “Women, Innovation and Impact” documents three years of implementation of the IP and Gender Action Plan (IPGAP), WIPO’s first strategy on IP in support of women and girls. It compiles stories under each of the IPGAP's three interconnected areas: helping governments integrate considerations for women into IP policy, legislation, and institutional practice; building the evidence base that makes the case for progress through data collection and research; and delivering direct support to women entrepreneurs, innovators, and creators through IP strategy, business development, and economic empowerment programs. The stories are a representative selection, chosen to reflect the breadth of achievements across regions, sectors, and areas of work, while underlining the remaining work. Taken together, this resource constitutes a call for more urgent and ambitious action to ensure that women's contributions are represented more fully in the global IP ecosystem.

title: Thanks, Trump: Why Canada may become the European Union’s first ever ‘associate member’
content:
Can a country change continents? Canada seems set to try.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has announced an intention to seek some novel form of associate membership in the European Union. It’s no mere flight of fancy, either, as Ursula von der Leyen, president of the EU Commission, has already endorsed the idea.

It’s a proposal that manages to be both absurd and eminently logical, depending on how you frame it. Geographically, Canada remains firmly affixed to North America, sharing a border with its increasingly unpredictable neighbour to the south, the United States.

In other important ways, however, Canada clearly has much more in common in recent months with European countries than the unstable U.S. That’s because in the space of a year, America has gone from Canada’s most important friend and ally on the world stage to the clearest threat to Canadian sovereignty.

By deepening links with other European democracies, Carney clearly hopes to buy Canada a degree of insurance against continuing American intervention and hostility from U.S. President Donald Trump. There’s a logic to the argument.

title: Rakkautta ja Anarkiaa -festari alkaa – Katso tästä Maailman Kuvalehden tärpit
content:
Singaporelaisen dokumentaristin ja tanssielokuvantekijän Chan Sze-Wein ohjaama 10s Across The Borders esittelee Kaakkois-Aasian ballroom-skenen vastustamattoman energisesti ja kauniisti. Koreografina ja tanssijana toiminut ohjaaja antaa paljon tilaa tanssille. 

Seitsemän vuoden ajan kuvattu tanssillinen dokumentti liikkuu Malesiassa, Filippiineillä ja Thaimaassa, jossa yhä uudet nuoret löytävät ballroom-kulttuurin ja vogue-tanssin ja kokevat ne omakseen. 

Yhteisöön päätyy usein nuoria, jotka ovat perheensä karsastamia tai hylkäämiä sukupuolensa ja seksuaalisen suuntautumisensa vuoksi. Paikallinen ballroom-skene tarjoaa monille uuden valitun perheen, joka antaa turvaa ja mahdollisuuden ilmaista itseään ja kasvaa. 

Dokumentin päähenkilöt korostavat antavansa arvoa ballroom-kulttuurin yhdysvaltalaisille pioneereille. He eivät halua omia kulttuuria, vaan omistautua sille.  

Itsekin lgbtqia+-yhteisöä edustava ohjaaja pääsee henkilöitään lähelle. Katsoja saa seurata päähenkilöiden matkaa New Yorkiin, jossa he pääsevät kansainväliselle catwalkille näyttämään kaiken osaamisensa – ja kokevat tulleensa tervetulleiksi ja hyväksytyiksi. 

Chan Sze-Wei: 10s Across The Borders (2025). Esitysajat täällä.

title: Putin’s United Russia will win – but vote tally, turnout and level of coercion will tell the real story of Russia’s wartime elections
content:
Russia’s parliamentary elections will take place on Sept. 18-20, 2026, amid the ongoing war with Ukraine. Given the backdrop of an energy crisis, battlefield failures in Ukraine and fears of more national conscription at home, you might think that the Kremlin should have reason for concern.

Yet few observers believe the result is in doubt: Russian President Vladimir Putin’s United Russia party will undoubtedly win. Anything less will demonstrate societal disloyalty to the government and opposition to the Ukraine War. And the Kremlin will not allow that.

In 2020, I wrote a book that demonstrated how the Kremlin does not have to engage in massive vote fraud to win a parliamentary majority. Russia’s election managers have consistently used coercive tactics and pressured business and bureaucratic managers to ensure workers support the government.

To me, the real indicators of public support for the government are the vote margin for Putin’s party and the extent to which the Kremlin places its thumb on the scale to maintain its party’s two-thirds majority of parliamentary seats.

title: Ikäihmisten päivätoimintaa ei saa siirtää kokonaan ruudun taakse
content:
Lapin hyvinvointialue on selvittämässä ikäihmisten päivätoiminnan siirtämistä kokonaan etätoiminnaksi. Tätä SDP:n valtuustoryhmä ei voi hyväksyä.

Ikäihmisten päivätoiminta on paljon enemmän kuin palvelu. Se on kohtaamisia, yhteisöllisyyttä, osallisuutta ja mahdollisuus olla osa ympäröivää yhteiskuntaa.

Etäpalvelut voivat täydentää päivätoimintaa ja parantaa saavutettavuutta, mutta ne eivät voi korvata ihmisten välistä vuorovaikutusta. Monille ikäihmiselle päivätoiminta on tärkeä osa arkea, hyvinvointia ja sosiaalisia suhteita. Kasvokkain tapahtuvat kohtaamiset ehkäisevät yksinäisyyttä, tukevat toimintakykyä ja vahvistavat yhteisöön kuulumisen tunnetta.

Jokaisella ikäihmisellä on oikeus tulla kohdatuksi ja osallistua yhteisöön riippumatta toimintakyvystään tai digitaidoistaan. Yksinäisyyden ehkäisy onkin merkittävä syy säilyttää päivätoiminta livenä. Se on inhimillinen kysymys, mutta yksinäisyys lisää merkittävästi myös ikäihmisten tarvetta terveydenhuoltopalveluille. Lisäksi päivätoiminta voi olla ainoa hetki, kun iäkäs omaishoitaja voi hetken hengähtää. Jos tätä mahdollisuutta ei ole, tulee tarve muulle sijaispalveluille. Kustannukset saattavat kokonaisuudessaan siis nousta.

title: Mieli ry: Ikääntyneiden elämänkokemus on alihyödynnetty voimavara
content:
Suomalaisessa yhteiskunnassa ikääntyminen nähdään julkisessa keskustelussa yhä usein uhkakuvana – taakkana, joka rasittaa palvelujärjestelmää ja huoltosuhdetta. Mielenterveysjärjestö MIELI ry haluaa kääntää katseen toisin päin: ikääntyneiden vuosikymmenten aikana karttunut selviytymiskyky voisi olla merkittävä voimavara koko yhteiskunnalle, mutta sitä hyödynnetään toistaiseksi liian vähän.

"Iäkkäillä on kokemusta siitä, miten vaikeita aikoja kohdataan ja miten niiden kanssa eletään. Se voisi olla yhteiskunnan voimavara ja kannatella yhteisöjä", sanoo MIELI ry:n johtava asiantuntija Sirkkaliisa Heimonen tiedotteessa.

Kielteiset mielikuvat ikääntymisestä elävät sitkeästi, vaikka tutkimustieto kertoo toista. THL:n ja Ikäinstituutin vuonna 2023 julkaiseman raportin mukaan valtaosa ikääntyneistä kokee itsensä onnelliseksi. Parhaiten mielen hyvinvointia raportoivat 65–74-vuotiaat, ja hyvinvointi alkaa laskea vasta myöhemmin – raportin mukaan miehillä noin 80 ja naisilla noin 75 ikävuoden jälkeen. Silloinkin yli puolet voi tutkimuksen mukaan edelleen vähintään kohtuullisesti.

Heimosen mukaan puhe pelkästä toimintakyvyn heikkenemisestä hämärtää helposti sen, mitä ikääntyneillä on annettavaa.

    Puheenvuorossaan 16.9. von der Leyen esitteli unionin tavoitteita, uusia avauksia ja aloitteita, joita EU:ssa ryhdytään edistämään. Puheen pääviesti oli selkeä: Euroopan on vahvistettava omaa toimintakykyään tilanteessa, jossa turvallisuusympäristö on muuttunut, teknologinen kilpailu kiihtyy ja riippuvuudet ulkopuolisista toimijoista ovat todellinen riski. Eurooppa on itsenäinen toimija, ja Euroopan on kyettävä toimimaan omilla ehdoillaan yhä epävarmemmassa maailmassa.

title: Linux’s 35th Anniversary and the Open Frontier
content:
Dear OSI community,

I’d be remiss if I didn’t open by wishing Linux a happy 35th birthday. I can’t pretend to have accomplished nearly as much by the age of 35 as Linux has, but neither was I nurtured by such a vast community of contributors and supporters. We can’t lose sight of that. Open Source is what it is because of the people who led us here, and keep us here. We all joined the community for different reasons, but many of us stayed because of the relationships and partnerships we built along the way, connections that run deeper than the code.

I get asked almost every day about the future of Open Source. One of my consistent answers is that people who love writing code will keep wanting to write code together. I believe that’s as true today as it was before AI tools, Git, the OSI, the World Wide Web, Perl, or C entered the chat. But we’re also passing through a moment of unquestionable transition. AI tools and agents are testing our processes, policies, laws, licenses, and beliefs in real time.

title: Everyday Products, Big Risks: China’s Connected Tech Danger
content:
Chinese ZPMC cranes supplied to American ports contained cellular modems that could bypass firewalls, gather information, and disrupt cargo handling. Chinese Yutong buses sold to Oslo came with connected battery and power controls. The Norwegian city’s public transport authority, Ruter, warned that, in theory, the buses “can be stopped or rendered inoperable by the manufacturer.”

Chinese connected vehicles carry cameras, microphones, and location sensors that gather data. Chinese-supplied apps, such as Hikvision’s Hik-Connect, send phone and SIM card identifiers to Chinese servers.

The West long has identified Chinese-supplied telecoms as a danger. It must now wake up and confront the danger of a vast array of Chinese products, ranging from cranes to cameras. Allies need to avoid instituting counterproductive sovereignty requirements. They should build a shared response that limits exposure by private purchase of Chinese consumer goods.

title: Inside the Heritage Month campaign to fill Wikipedia’s language void, one article at a time
content:
The instruction was simple, and Matete Lesele had given it many times. Choose an article on the English Wikipedia, he told the students in front of him, and translate it into the language you grew up speaking. Most reached for the wiki in their mother tongue. This student reached for Afrikaans; not her mother tongue. When he pointed her back toward her own language, she told him she couldn’t write it — the school she had gone to never taught her how.

Lesele, a librarian at the City of Johannesburg and a board member of Wikimedia South Africa, repeats some version of that exchange to almost everyone who asks why he does this work. It was the moment a vague worry turned specific. A language can live in conversation, in songs, in the things a grandmother says that no one writes down. But a person who cannot write their own language is unlikely to add it to the places people now go to look — and the largest of those, by a distance hard to overstate, is the one he spends his evenings inside.

content:
Kansallisarkisto luopuu Jyväskylän toimipaikasta 1.1.2027 lukien, kuten aiemmin on tiedotettu.

Tutkijasalipalvelu Jyväskylän toimipaikassa päättyy 29.9.2026. Toimipaikan tutkijasali on avoinna syyskuussa vielä seuraavasti:

  • tiistaina 22.9. kello 9–16
  • tiistaina 29.9. kello 9–16.

    • Lisäksi luvanvarainen itsepalveluasiointi on mahdollista 23.–24. syyskuuta klo 9–16.

    Siirtojen aikana aineistoihin voi tehdä tietopyyntöjä, eli niistä voi tilata kopioita tai todistuksia, mutta toimitusaika voi olla normaalia pidempi.

    Siirtojen jälkeen aineistot ovat asiakkaiden käytettävissä uusissa säilyttävissä toimipaikoissa seuraavasti:

title: Uusi maisteriohjelma tarjoaa ruokaviennin kansainvälistä osaamista
content:
The English-language Master’s Programme in International Food Business and Gastronomy equips students with relevant skills in branding, export, gastronomy and sustainability. 

This two-year programme centres on international food business including management and marketing, and covers sustainable food systems, logistics and food legislation. In addition, students learn to understand gastronomic markets, develop new gastronomy products and services and introduce them to new markets. 

Graduates from the programme can pursue careers in international food companies, working, for instance, as brand and product, export or marketing managers. Other options include key account management roles in retail, or setting up one’s own food-sector startup.

While the expertise developed also applies well to NGOs, public-sector organisations and research institutes involved in food systems, the programme equally prepares students for postgraduate study and academic careers.

title: Watch Footage from the Psychology Experiment That Shocked the World: Milgram’s Obedience Study (1961)
content:
For decades following World War II,  the world was left wondering how the atrocities of the Holocaust could have been perpetrated in the midst of—and, most horrifically, by—a modern and civilized society. How did people come to engage in a willing and systematic extermination of their neighbors? Psychologists, whose field had grown into a grudgingly respected science by the midpoint of the 20th century, were eager to tackle the question.

In 1961, Yale University’s Stanley Milgram began a series of infamous obedience experiments. While Adolf Eichmann’s trial was underway in Jerusalem (resulting in Hannah Arendt’s five-piece reportage, which became one of The New Yorker magazine’s most dramatic and controversial article series), Milgram began to suspect that human nature was more straightforward than earlier theorists had imagined; he wondered, as he later wrote, “Could it be that Eichmann and his million accomplices in the Holocaust were just following orders? Could we call them all accomplices?”

title: Victory: Court, Using a New Test, Rules Embedding Links is Legal
content:
Courts have for two decades found that linking and embedding someone else’s web content, be it a photo, music, or an article, doesn’t violate copyright law–the entity that controls the server that hosts a copyrighted work, not the user or website that merely directs others to it, is directly liable if the content turns out to be infringing.

News publisher Emmerich Newspapers sought to convince the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals to chart a new and dangerous course, arguing that an aggregator website that published links to its copyrighted articles was in effect “displaying” them and can be directly liable for infringement. EFF, along with several other public interest organizations and trade associations, filed a brief urging the court to follow multiple other circuits and reject that theory.

Fortunately, the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals did just that. While it rejected the server test–the rule courts have used to determine copyright liability rests with whoever serves up the content–the court came to the same practical conclusion by focusing on who is responsible for transmitting content.

title: ‘The US can’t lose’: Pentagon plows ahead on AI despite warnings
content:
Pentagon leaders are racing to insert artificial intelligence into nearly every corner of the military, even as lawmakers scramble to figure out guardrails.

Defense Department officials insist any slowdown in AI development could cede control to adversaries, dismissing calls from industry leaders and members of Congress to pause and better understand the long-term ramifications of the computer systems.

That tension is playing out in real time as the Pentagon faces increasingly bold threats from China and Russia. But the military’s rush to stay ahead brings separate risks if it fails to safeguard hastily implemented AI tech.

“Winning and staying ahead in the AI race is probably one of the most important things for the United States to do, both from a military and economic security perspective,” Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said. “That is a race that the U.S. can’t lose.”

But critics warn the rush to use advanced AI in national security operations could also open sensitive military systems to new threats, especially if leaders aren’t deliberate about installing defenses during upgrades.

title: Rahim Molaeian Sentenced to Prison by Revolutionary Court
content:
According to HRANA, Rahim Molaeian has been sentenced to prison.

Under a ruling issued on Sunday, September 13, by Branch 1 of the Babol Revolutionary Court, Mr. Molaeian was sentenced to six months in prison on the charge of “propaganda against the regime.”

According to information received by HRANA, Molaeian’s paintings and posts he shared as Instagram Stories were cited as evidence supporting the charge against him.

A hearing on the charge was held before the same branch on September 6 of this year.

In April-May of this year, his office, studio, and residence were searched by 12 security agents, and 28 of Molaeian’s paintings were confiscated for 48 hours. In connection with the case, Mr. Molaeian was also interrogated by security agencies on three occasions, with each session lasting four hours.

Rahim Molaeian, 66, is a painter and sculptor from Babol, where he currently resides. He is married and the father of three children.

title: Reforms to Hungary's Anti-LGBT Laws Welcome, but More to Do
content:
Hungary’s new government has taken an important step toward dismantling a key discriminatory legacy of the Orbán era—the legal targeting of LGBT people. The job is not finished, however.

The government submitted legislation to Parliament on September 14 to remove several provisions of the 2021 so-called “child protection” law that restrict the “portrayal” or “promotion” of sexual and gender diversity in content accessible to children. The proposed changes remove the restrictions from laws relating to child protection, media, advertising, and education.

The reforms follow an April judgment by the Court of Justice of the European Union finding that Hungary’s legal restrictions stigmatized and marginalized LGBT people and violated EU law. The court found that Hungary could not invoke the best interests of the child to justify restrictions that discriminated against LGBT people and violated fundamental rights.

title: Brussels: Demonstration Place du Luxembourg for Eritrean Refugees Detained in Libya
content:
By Cedric Stephany | BRUSSELS, Belgium | 16 September 2026 (IDN) — Around 750 to 1000 people gathered on Saturday, September 12, at Place du Luxembourg in Brussels. The demonstration, held in front of the European Parliament, demanded the release of Eritrean refugees held in detention centres in Benghazi and Tajoura, Libya, and to call for stronger protection measures from European and international institutions.

Organised by members of the Eritrean diaspora, the protest ran from 12 p.m. to 2 p.m. Protesters held signs reading “Free the Refugees in Libya” and “STOP hate! Protect Human Life!” alongside messages denouncing the situation facing Eritrean refugees in Libya.

A petition, detention centres and a name behind the numbers

title: Amnesty: 87 Iranin viranomaista saatettava vastuuseen rikoksista ihmisyyttä vastaan
content:
Amnesty paljastaa tänään julkaistavassa raportissaan (liitteenä), miten vuoden 2022 Woman Life Freedom -mielenosoitusten verisestä tukahduttamisesta vastuussa olevat henkilöt johtavat edelleen maan tappavaa sortokoneistoa.

Raportti Architects of Atrocities: State Machinery Orchestrating Crimes Against Humanity in Iran’s 2022 Woman Life Freedom Uprising kuvaa yksityiskohtaisesti, kuinka Iranin viranomaiset tappoivat, kiduttivat, raiskasivat ja vangitsivat ihmisiä mielenosoitusten tukahduttamiseksi. Lisäksi järjestö analysoi yli 2 000 videota sekä laajaa aineistoa, kuten viranomaisten lausuntoja, vuotaneita virallisia asiakirjoja, syyttäjien määräyksiä, tuomioistuinratkaisuja ja oikeuslääketieteellisiä asiakirjoja.

title: French Prosecutors Seek Up to 5 Years in Prison for Sons of Ex-Yemeni President Saleh Over Ill-Gotten Assets
content:
Two sons of late Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh could face up to five years in prison as a Paris court hears charges against them for allegedly laundering tens of millions of euros in embezzled state funds and corruption proceeds.

The trial, which opened September 7 at the Paris Criminal Court, follows a 2019 investigation launched by France's National Financial Prosecutor's Office (PNF) based on a tip-off from Swiss authorities, the PNF confirmed to OCCRP on Wednesday.

Brothers Ahmed Ali Saleh, 54, and Khaled Ali Saleh, 39, are accused of laundering proceeds from corruption and laundering embezzled public funds as part of an organized criminal group. Both men are being tried in absentia and are believed to be residing in Dubai.

Their father, Ali Abdullah Saleh, ruled Yemen for 33 years until his ouster during the Arab Spring in 2012. The former president was accused of plundering billions in state funds throughout his long tenure to enrich his family and inner circle. He was killed by Houthi rebels in 2017.

title: Arizona Lowered the Bar for Its English Fluency Test. Experts Say It Will Harm Students in the Long Run.
content:
Samantha Ramos stood at the front of her second grade classroom, a small mic clipped to her lanyard amplifying her instructions as she began a phonics lesson.

“Can we get our arms ready?” asked Ramos, who’s taught at the John B. Wright Elementary School in Tucson, Arizona, for 15 years. She brought her right palm to her left shoulder as the students imitated her movements.

Ramos, who specializes in teaching English as a second language, was leading a lesson that day on the short “i” sound. She told the students to pronounce each letter with a different gesture — touching the shoulder for the “w,” the elbow for the “i” and the hand for the double “l” — before sounding out the word “will.” They repeated the process for other short “i” words — “dig,” “wig” and “fit.”

title: Rapid Houthi advances in Yemen pose massive strategic risks for Saudi Arabia in the Gulf
content:
An advance by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, which has included the targeting of Saudi cities and infrastructure, has quickly complicated a widening Middle East war.

Not only has it all but unraveled a 2022 truce putting a lid on Yemen’s civil war – in which the Iran-aligned Houthis were fighting a Saudi-led coalition – but the seizure of territory next to the Red Sea has further threatened Saudi energy exports. On Sept. 13, Saudi Arabia and other Arab Gulf nations were due to take part in crucial Omani-hosted talks with Iran in a bid to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. But they were called off, seemingly over attacks by both the Houthis and Iraqi groups aligned with Tehran.

The Conversation spoke with Gulf analyst Kristian Coates Ulrichsen to help make sense of the dizzying array of intersecting news developments.

Periodically since the war in Iran began on Feb. 28, 2026, and particularly since the signing of the Iran-U.S. memorandum of understanding in mid-June, Omani and Iranian officials have been meeting to discuss how to resolve the blockage in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Haagista kova tuomio Kosovon ex-presidentille – 25 vuotta vankeutta sotarikoksista
content:
Kosovon entinen presidentti Hashim Thaci on tuomittu 25 vuodeksi vankeuteen sotarikoksista Haagissa sotarikosoikeudenkäynnissä.

Oikeudenkäynti kesti kolme vuotta. Tuomarit totesivat tuomiossaan Thacin syyllistyneen laittomiin pidätyksiin, kidutukseen, murhiin ja julmaan kohteluun.

Tuomion odotetaan herättävän raivoa Balkanin maissa, sillä Thaci on monien kosovolaisten silmissä sankari. Kosovon pääkaupungissa Pristinassa väkijoukko kokoontui seuraamaan tuomion julistamista suurilta näytöiltä suorana lähetyksenä. Tuomion kuultuaan väkijoukko vaipui hiljaisuuteen. Monet näyttivät olevan järkyttyneitä päätöksestä.

Thaci toimi Kosovon vapautusarmeijan UCK:n johtajana Kosovon itsenäisyyssodan aikana vuodesta 1998 vuoteen 1999. Kosovon presidenttinä hän toimi vuodesta 2016 vuoteen 2020. Thaci erosi presidentin virasta saatuaan syytteen sotarikoksista.

Syytettyinä oli myös kolme muuta entisen Kosovon vapautusarmeijan johtajaa, jotka todettiin niin ikään syyllisiksi. Jakup Krasniqi tuomittiin 25 vuodeksi vankeuteen, Rexhep Selimi sai 13 vuoden tuomion ja Kadri Veseli 18 vuoden tuomion.

title: Älä uuvu, aktivisti – jonain päivänä sinua saatetaan tarvita vastarintaan
content:
Johanna Kohvakka

Maailman tilasta ahdistuneelle ihmiselle voi suositella yhtä hieman epätavanomaista harjoitusta: ajattele maailmaa muutaman miljardin vuoden perspektiivillä.

Lopputulos on nimittäin jo tiedossa.

Auringon ikääntyessä sen säteilyteho hitaasti kasvaa. Noin kahden miljardin vuoden kuluttua lisääntyvä lämpö alkaa haihduttaa Maan valtameriä, ja planeetan pinnasta tulee nykyisenkaltaiselle elämälle elinkelvoton. Noin viiden miljardin vuoden kuluttua Aurinko paisuu punaiseksi jättiläiseksi. Se nielaisee varmasti Merkuriuksen ja Venuksen ja saattaa nielaista myös Maan – joka tapauksessa Maa on siinä vaiheessa ollut elinkelvoton jo miljardeja vuosia.

Maailmanlopun suhteen voimme siis rentoutua hieman. Se hoitaa kyllä itse itsensä, aikataulussa, ilman meidän apuamme.

Paljon vaikeampi kysymys on, mitä teemme siihen asti.

Ympäristökriisin yksi psykologisesti raskaimmista puolista on seurata, kuinka suuri osa ihmisistä näyttää jatkavan elämäänsä aivan kuin mitään erityistä ei olisi tapahtumassa.

title: Ei vain tahroja paperilla – visiot auttavat johtamaan muutosta
content:
• Etusivu

    • Blogi

    Suomi on vaikean kaksoishaasteen edessä. Taloutta on toisaalta sopeutettava nopeasti ja toisaalta uudistettava pitkäjänteisesti. Näiden tarpeiden yhdistäminen edellyttää yhteistä käsitystä Suomen suunnasta. Apua kannattaa hakea visioista, sillä ne auttavat tekemään valintoja.

    Asiantuntija, Ennakointi ja koulutus

    Blogi

    Julkaistu

    16.9.2026

    Tänä syksynä Suomi-rockin jättiläinen Eppu Normaali lopetti 50 vuotta jatkuneen uransa. ”Tarhoja paperilla” on yksi yhtyeen tunnetuimmista kappaleista. Sen lyriikoihin tiivistyy myös monien epäluulo visioita kohtaan: ne ovat vain tahroja paperilla eikä niistä asiat miksikään muutu.

    Kriitikot ovat oikeassa siinä, että visiot eivät itsessään ratkaise Suomen talouden tai yhteiskunnan ongelmia. Silti Suomi tarvitsee visioita kipeämmin kuin pitkään aikaan.

    Visiot ovat talouspolitiikan johtamisen ja toimeenpanon työkaluja. Ne voivat osoittautua erityisen hyödylliseksi Suomen historiallisen vaikean kaksoishaasteen äärellä.

    Yhtäältä on sopeuduttava mahdollisimman nopeasti julkisen talouden, väestörakenteen ja turvallisuusympäristön asettamiin reunaehtoihin ja pidettävä yllä valmiutta reagoida yllätyksiin.

title: Analysis: Global fossil-fuel emissions set to fall in 2026 amid Hormuz crisis
content:
Global fossil-fuel emissions are set to fall by around 0.5% in 2026 amid the fallout from the Hormuz crisis, according to Carbon Brief analysis.

The US-Iran war has severely disrupted trade through the strait of Hormuz, causing a spike in oil and gas prices that continues to ripple around the global economy.

Each month of disruption – and each new flashpoint, such as in Yemen – is increasing the incentive to switch to alternatives.

Those alternatives include coal, with the latest forecasts pointing to a 1.2% rise in coal demand this year – apparently supporting media claims of a “return to coal” in the wake of the crisis.

Yet Carbon Brief’s analysis shows the rise in emissions associated with this increased coal use, much of which is unrelated to Hormuz, is set to be more than offset by declines for oil and gas.

The estimated overall impact on carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from fossil fuels in 2026 is shown in the figure below and amounts to a reduction of around 0.5% from 2025 levels.

(Fossil fuels account for two-thirds of global greenhouse gas emissions.)

title: Open Weights Are Good. Open Source Is Better.
content:
By this point, you’ve seen the news about open-weight AI models and the debate over their security, efficiency, and impact on both local and national economies. Scores of businesses have come out in support of open-weights, highlighting how they increase access to advanced AI and maintain competition in the market. This is all true, and shedding light on these arguments benefits the Open Source community. 

At the same time, we must take this moment, when openness in AI is making headlines, to educate policymakers, producers, and users of these technologies about what open-weight and Open Source AI mean for the four software freedoms: the freedom to use, study, modify, and share without the need to ask for permission from the rights holder. Those are the core tenets of the Open Source movement that power the technology we use every day. Those are the tenets that built the Open Source ecosystem with a demand-side value of $8.8 trillion. It’s those tenets that we should strive to uphold in this next phase of technological development.

title: Leveraging knowledge management to enhance research access and visibility via institutional repositories in South African universities
content: Abstract: Purpose – This study aims to examine how South African universities are applying knowledge management practices to enhance the effectiveness of institutional repositories in improving research access and visibility. Design/methodology/approach – The research was conducted using a qualitative content analysis, gathering data from secondary sources and organising it according to the stages of knowledge management: knowledge capture, organisation and storage, dissemination and application. Findings – All universities in South Africa have implemented repositories, yet their alignment with knowledge management outcomes is lacking. Poor alignment between repository goals and knowledge management outcomes, limited institutional support, fragmentation and siloed practices contributed to the underutilisation of repository systems. title: Ukraine Advances: The Tank Isn’t Finished Yet
content:
Ukraine’s 3 Army Corps, acting under strict operational silence, has been conducting a counterattack in the Lyman sector for months. The cloud of secrecy has now been lifted, and Russian forces have lost a significant amount of territory. The operation, named Vivaldi, has so far officially cleared 75 sq km (29 sq miles), Ukrainian forces say. It is not yet over.

“In Vivaldi, as you know, there are four seasons,” Brig. Gen. Andriy Biletsky said on September 15. “And this is only the first . . . Good news is coming.”

Russia’s leadership had hoped to encircle Ukraine’s formidable fortress belt in western Donbas, but the northern salient has been reduced, with Russian warbloggers claiming it will extend the battle for Donbas by a year. Credible independent sources say the Ukrainian territorial gain is even greater.

title: ‘Godfather of AI’ says tech regulation is nearing Covid-style pivot moment
content:
Safety crisis makes it more likely that governments will be spurred into action, says Yoshua Bengio

Concerns over AI safety are reaching a point where governments realise they must act to protect the public, similarly to in the Covid pandemic, according to one of the “godfathers” of the technology.

Yoshua Bengio said recent events, including a “swarm” of OpenAI agents hacking a startup and tech insider warnings of an existential threat, were cutting through – making government action more likely.

title: Tieteen vapaus on heikentynyt Suomessa – eduskuntavaaleissa valitaan suunta
content:
Suomen asema tieteen vapauden kärkimaana on heikentynyt. Tutkijoiden työhön kohdistuu aiempaa enemmän häirintää, ja tutkimuksen poliittinen ja taloudellinen ohjaus on vahvistunut. Samaan aikaan ekologinen kriisi ja muut turvallisuusuhat, huoli taloudesta ja disinformaatio kasvattavat riippumattoman tutkitun tiedon tarvetta.

Kevään 2027 eduskuntavaaleissa valitaan päättäjät, jotka ratkaisevat myös sen, millaiset edellytykset Suomessa annetaan uuden tiedon syntymiselle. Äänestäjät voivat vaatia ehdokkailta selkeitä vastauksia: miten he puolustavat tieteen ja tutkijoiden vapautta, turvaavat tutkimuksen pitkäjänteisen rahoituksen ja vahvistavat tutkitun tiedon asemaa päätöksenteossa?

Joukko tiedekentän keskeisiä toimijoita tuo nämä kysymykset vaalikeskusteluun Vapaa tiede ratkaisee -kampanjalla. Kampanja tuo esiin sen, kuinka tärkeää tieteen vapaudesta ja resursseista huolehtiminen on monikriisin keskellä.

Tulevalla vaalikaudella on tehtävä selkeä valinta: panostetaanko vapaaseen tieteeseen vai tingitäänkö toivosta.

title: EFF Welcomes Alexander Macgillivray to its Board of Directors
content:
The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) is honored to announce today that Alexander “amac” Macgillivray — a former White House official who also served in top legal capacities at Twitter and Google — has joined EFF’s Board of Directors. 

Macgillivray served in the Biden Administration as Deputy Assistant to the President and Principal Deputy U.S. Chief Technology Officer in the Office of Science and Technology Policy, and earlier had held a similar position in the Obama Administration. Macgillivray was one of the co-authors of the Biden Administration’s Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights and oversaw many of the Administration’s AI initiatives, such as organizing its AI CEO convening, leading its working group on federal AI policy, and overseeing the creation of the National AI Research and Development Strategic Plan and National AI Research Resource. 

He was Twitter's General Counsel from 2009 to 2013, leading the Corporate Development, Public Policy, Communications, and Trust & Safety teams. Before that he was Deputy General Counsel at Google from 2003 to 2009, where he created the Product Counsel team.

title: Hugging Face CEO: Advanced AI models require new transparency mandates
content:
The CEO whose company fell victim to history’s first known autonomous artificial intelligence cyberattack said the government should do more to require transparency by advanced AI models — and ensure that their developers are held liable for harms their products cause.

That doesn’t mean Congress needs to create a raft of new regulations prohibiting malicious cyberattacks, Hugging Face CEO and co-founder Clem Delangue said Wednesday during the POLITICO Decoded Summit in D.C. But he said companies whose products inflict damage should not be able to dodge responsibility.

“I think it’s too easy to say: ‘OK, it was an agent. That did the bad thing and so no one is responsible,’” Delangue said. “It doesn’t work, in my opinion, because if you say that you’re going to end up in a world where everyone’s agent is attacking everyone’s with no clear kind of responsibility.”

He declined to comment on some specific legislation, including an AI liability proposal in California but said the government has a role to play in mandating disclosures of cyber incidents.

title: Why is Amnesty International calling for international justice for crimes against humanity in Iran?
content:
Content warning: This article contains descriptions of violence, including shootings, beatings, torture, sexual violence, and discrimination. It also mentions issues relating to suicide. We include these details to honour the victims and their families, who want the truth to be brought to light.

Protesters in Iran have been killed, tortured or imprisoned in the thousands for demanding their human rights and political change. The officials responsible for protest-related crimes against humanity are evading justice while survivors and relatives seeking justice are persecuted.

In late 2022, Iran was gripped by large-scale protests that became known as the Woman Life Freedom uprising. After years of painstaking investigations, Amnesty International has exposed how the Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity to crush the uprising. Based on its extensive documentation of the crimes committed and analysis of the security forces’ command structures, Amnesty International has identified 87 officials who must be criminally investigated for their role in these crimes.

title: Teachers’ Union Activist Masoud Farhikhteh Sentenced to Additional Prison Term in New Case
content:
According to HRANA, citing the Coordinating Council of Iranian Teachers’ Trade Associations, Masoud Farhikhteh has been sentenced to prison and additional punishments.

According to the report, Ramin Safarnia, Mr. Farhikhteh’s attorney, stated that the teachers’ union activist was sentenced to one year in prison on the charge of “propaganda against the regime.” As additional punishments, he was also sentenced to a two-year ban on leaving the country, a two-year ban on membership in political and social parties, groups, and organizations, and dismissal from government and public service.

The report states that the ruling was based on a report by judicial officers at Karaj Central Penitentiary.

In this new case, which was opened against Mr. Farhikhteh during his incarceration, he was summoned to the Karaj Revolutionary Court after the completion of the interrogation stage.

In July of this year, Masoud Farhikhteh was transferred from Ward 16 of Karaj Central Penitentiary to solitary confinement. He was also deprived of telephone calls and visits with his family after publishing statements concerning prisoners’ demands.

title: The Significance of The Enemy States Clause for Germany
content:
By Michael von der Schulenburg

BRUSSELS | 16 September 2026 (IDN) — When the Allies of the Second World War drafted the United Nations Charter, they sought to establish a global system of collective security. Its aim was to “save succeeding generations from the scourge of war”. With the adoption of the UN Charter, all UN Member States undertook to settle their disputes in future exclusively by peaceful means, and not through military force. Decisions on the use of force to maintain or restore peace were only to be taken collectively, initially by the eleven and now by the fifteen members of the United Nations Security Council.

However, the UN Charter contains an exception that has been largely forgotten today: the so-called ‘enemy states clause’ in Articles 53, 77 and 107. It grants the former Allied powers the right to take military action against the enemy states of the former Axis powers, without a Security Council mandate, in order to prevent renewed aggression by those states against them. Because the Security Council is expressly excluded, each former Ally could assess whether a former Axis power was once again adopting an aggressive stance.

title: Al-Qaida and IS-linked violence in Africa’s Sahel belt set to hit record levels this year
content:
Twenty-five years after 9/11, figures compiled by conflict monitor underline how Sahel region has become centre of Islamist terror

Islamist extremist violence in Africa’s Sahel region is set to reach historic highs after a series of sweeping offensives by groups linked to al-Qaida and Islamic State, according to new figures compiled by the conflict monitor Acled.

As the US marks the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks launched by al-Qaida against targets in Washington and New York, the statistics underline the continued expansion of the veteran organisation in parts of Africa – in stark contrast with its relative weakness elsewhere.

title: From Fugitive to Federal Custody: Inside the Takedown of South America’s ‘King of the South’
content:
When federal agents reached out to Sebastián Marset through his girlfriend in March 2025 to persuade him to surrender, the Uruguayan drug lord who styled himself the “King of the South” mocked them, boasting that he was "smarter than the entire D.E.A. put together."

“I’m not going to surrender,” Marset declared, according to court records. “I’ll be a criminal for the rest of my life.”

Almost a year later, heavily armed Bolivian special forces raided a residential neighborhood in Santa Cruz in the pre-dawn hours, capturing the fugitive who had evaded international law enforcement for years.

By that evening, one of the most powerful drug barons in South America’s Southern Cone - wanted by federal prosecutors for laundering millions of dollars in illicit proceeds through American banks - landed on U.S. soil in handcuffs.

Now held in a federal detention center in Virginia, Marset is mounting an aggressive legal defense. A new series of court filings has laid bare a detailed record of his global operations, missing evidence, and his own cynical view of regional law enforcement.

title: Meta is changing Instagram and Facebook to protect teens’ mental health. Are the new measures backed up by science?
content:
The recent landmark ruling against Meta in the United States was the result of a lawsuit filed in 2023 which went to trial in August 2026. It was brought by nearly fifty attorneys general, school districts and families, who alleged that the company’s social media platforms, which include Instagram and Facebook, pose serious risks to mental health.

The case ended in a $18 billion dollar settlement, and imposed direct structural changes on the way Instagram and Facebook operate. These could eventually extend to other platforms and social media networks, according to Attorney General William Tong.

Here, we will look at the scientific basis for each of the new measures.

Firstly, the agreement sets a limit of two hours’ use per day for under-18s, alongside regular reminders to encourage breaks and more self-regulated use.

Scientific research supports the general idea of limiting time spent on social media and encouraging breaks while using it. However, this does not make the two-hour limit a universal medical threshold, nor are the regular reminders scientifically established intervals.

title: Pardoned by Trump and escaping charges at home, ex-Honduran leader’s case shows a nation’s struggle for sovereignty
content:
A Honduran judge on Sept. 1, 2026, dismissed a sprawling money-laundering and fraud case against the country’s former president, Juan Orlando Hernández. It was the latest stroke of good fortune for Hernández.

Hernández returned home in late July after an eventful four years outside Honduras. He was extradited to the United States in 2022 following a multiyear, nonpartisan U.S. investigation. In 2024 he was convicted of cocaine trafficking and related charges and sentenced to 45 years behind bars in the U.S. Yet after serving only 18 months of his sentence, Hernández was pardoned by President Donald Trump.

Hernández remains a forceful power broker behind the scenes of the current Honduran government, led by President Nasry Asfura of the right-wing National Party.

Yet as a scholar of Latin American politics, I believe Hernández’s return to Honduras, and his successes evading legal accountability, are emblematic of something broader than impunity for elites: His case demonstrates the struggle for sovereignty in a country facing a renewed form of U.S. intervention.

title: Lentoposti: Ensimmäiset F-35-hävittäjät matkalla Suomeen
content:
Ilmavoimien ensimmäiset uudet F-35-hävittäjät ovat jo matkalla Suomeen, kertoi Lentoposti–uutissivusto keskiviikkona.

Sen mukaan siirtolento Yhdysvalloista Suomeen oli edennyt tiistaina Portugalille kuuluville Azorien saarille Atlantilla.

Paikalliset kuvaajat ikuistivat kolme Suomen F-35-hävittäjää, kun ne laskeutuivat lentotukikohtaan Azoreilla.

Samalla ilmatankkauskoneiden tukemalla siirtolennolla oli Lentopostin mukaan myös kolme Belgian ilmavoimille kuuluvaa hävittäjäkonetta.

ILMAVOIMAT ei ole paljastanut ensimmäisten koneiden tarkkaa saapumisaikataulua Suomeen. Uusia koneita esitellään mediatilaisuudessa Rovaniemellä 1. lokakuuta.

Suomi on päättänyt hankkia kaikkiaan 64 Lockheed Martinin valmistamaa F-35-hävittäjää Ilmavoimien nykyisten Hornetien seuraajiksi.

content:
Suomi myöntää 2,55 miljoonaa euroa Tyynenmeren saarivaltioiden ja Indonesian varautumiseen sään ääri-ilmiöihin. PACIDFIN-hankkeen toteutuksesta vastaa Suomen Ilmatieteen laitos yhdessä Tyynenmeren meteorologisen neuvoston ja Indonesian Ilmatieteen laitoksen kanssa.

PACIDFIN-hankkeen tavoitteena on parantaa Tyynenmeren saarivaltioiden ja Indonesian kykyä varautua ilmastonmuutoksen ja sään ääri-ilmiöihin kehittämällä sää-, ilmasto- ja ennakkovaroituspalveluja.

Alueen maat ovat haavoittuvia ilmastonmuutokselle ja sään ääri-ilmiöille. Hanke vastaa alueen merkittäviin haasteisiin, kuten kuivuuteen, tulviin ja elinkeinojen haavoittuvuuteen.

title: To sign or not to sign initiatives to reform research evaluation: A discussion of the pros and cons - ScienceDirect
content: Abstract: The integration of bibliometrics into science governance has fundamentally transformed scientific practices, leading to unintended consequences such as goal displacement and citizen bibliometrics. In response, international reform movements like the Agreement on Reforming Research Assessment (CoARA) advocate for responsible research assessment and the primacy of qualitative peer review. This short communication examines the commonalities and differences of these movements and weighs the pros and cons for research organizations considering signing them. While endorsement offers socio-political legitimacy and can catalyze internal modernization toward improved evaluation processes, organizations are also confronted with certain challenges. These include the potential neglect of disciplinary evaluation cultures, the high administrative burden of qualitative review, and the prevalent risk of purely symbolic uptake. Acknowledging the limitations of current empirical evidence, this commentary concludes that the future of research assessment relies not on universal declarations, but on the development of process-specific evaluation designs. title: Russia’s Neighbors Battle Oil Addiction
content:
Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Kazakhstan cut ties with the Soviet Union more than three decades ago, and have developed their own economies and foreign policies. Yet in the critical area of energy security, not much has changed; they remain heavily dependent on the Kremlin’s goodwill.

The crisis began to unfold this spring and summer, as Ukraine’s long-range drone attacks on Russia’s refineries got increasingly successful. On July 6, drones reached the Omsk refinery for the first time, some 2,700 km (1,700 miles) from the Ukrainian border, and Russia’s largest refining facility was forced to halt production.

Omsk, the eleventh major gasoline producer to be struck, was the principal supplier of petroleum products to Central Asia and Mongolia. And disruption followed as Moscow prioritized supplying its own regions with fuel.

While it was never part of the Soviet Union, Mongolia is the most vulnerable to the shock, as more than 90% of its petroleum products come from Russia. Lines formed at filling stations in Ulaanbaatar and significant restrictions on fuel sales were introduced.

title: Small but mighty! Remembering the GameCube, Nintendo’s purple box of delights
content:
The first console I ever bought, it was hyped as a threat to the PlayStation, then mocked as a flop. But now, as it marks its 25th anniversary, it’s looked back on with misty-eyed reverence

This week marks the 25th anniversary of the Nintendo GameCube, the first console I ever bought with my own money. I vividly remember getting on the bus after school with a year’s worth of savings safely zipped into the pocket of my bag and going to a branch of Currys, where I dumped a bunch of notes, coins and vouchers on the counter to collect my pre-order. (It turned out that some of the vouchers from the previous Christmas had expired, but the guy at the checkout clearly felt so sorry for me that he redeemed them anyway. If you’re out there, Currys guy: thank you for taking pity on a desperate 13-year-old.)

title: Lapissa on käynnistetty toimintakykyyn keskittyvän osaamiskeskuksen valmistelu
content:
Lapin ammattikorkeakoulussa kehitetään uutta Arktista toimintakykyosaamiskeskusta, jonka tavoitteena on vahvistaa toimintakykyyn liittyvää tutkimusta, kehittämistä, koulutusta ja yhteistyötä pohjoisissa olosuhteissa. Osaamiskeskus kokoaa yhteen asiantuntijat, tutkimus- ja kehittämistoiminnan sekä alueelliset, kansalliset ja kansainväliset verkostot.

Lapin ammattikorkeakoulussa on jo vuosien ajan tehty toimintakykyyn liittyvää tutkimus-, kehittämis- ja innovaatiotyötä (TKI). TKI-toiminnassa on kehitetty muun muassa kuntoutuksen vaikuttavuuden arviointia, sosiaalisen kuntoutuksen toimintamalleja sekä digitaalisia ja teknologia-avusteisia palveluja. Erityisesti harvaan asutut ja arktiset toimintaympäristöt ovat olleet kehittämistyön keskiössä.

Vuosien myötä kertyneen osaamisen pohjalle rakentuva Arktinen toimintakykyosaamiskeskus kokoaa yhteen tutkimuksen, verkostot ja palveluinnovaatiot yhdeksi laajasti hyödynnettäväksi kokonaisuudeksi.

Toimintakyky nähdään ammattikorkeakoululla kokonaisvaltaisena fyysisenä, psyykkisenä ja sosiaalisena ilmiönä, joka mahdollistaa osallisuuden, opiskelu- ja työkyvyn sekä arjessa selviytymisen.

title: Melartin-tutkija Tuire Ranta-Meyer vieraana Lahden pääkirjaston musiikkialueella 23.9.
content:
Vierailulla kuullaan musiikin säestämä katsaus säveltäjä Erkki Melartinin elämään ja työhön.

Lahden pääkirjaston musiikkialueen vieraaksi saapuu FT Tuire Ranta-Meyer, joka on kirjoittanut Erkki Melartinin elämänkerran. Ranta-Meyer kertoo tilaisuudessa Melartinista, kirjan synnystä sekä siitä, miksi hänen kiinnostuksensa Melartinin elämään ja tuotantoon on pysynyt yllä jo lähes 40 vuotta.

Niin nuori, niin palava – Erkki Melartinin elämä, työ ja musiikki julkaistiin vuonna 2025, jolloin tuli kuluneeksi 150 vuotta Melartinin syntymästä. Teos on ensimmäinen Melartinista kirjoitettu elämäkerta. Säveltäjän monia kiinnostuksen kohteita sisältäneen elämän vuoksi siitä kasvoi lähes 800-sivuinen.

Erkki Melartin (1875–1937) tunnetaan Juhlamarssin eli kansankielisesti Prinsessa Ruususen häämarssin säveltäjänä. Melartin sävelsi suomalaisen häämusiikin klassikon vuonna 1904 Zachris Topeliuksen samannimiseen satunäytelmään. Melartin oli aikansa tunnettu kulttuurivaikuttaja: säveltäjäntyön lisäksi kapellimestari, sävellyksenopettaja, Sibelius-Akatemian rehtori ja taidemaalari.

title: Anthropic policy chief says winning AI race key for safety
content:
Anthropic’s policy chief Sarah Heck said Wednesday that the U.S. can’t make artificial intelligence safer if it falls behind China in the global tech race.

“The United States needs to stay in the lead on AI, and you can’t do safety from second place,” the head of public policy said at POLITICO’s Decoded summit in Washington, echoing an argument often made by President Donald Trump and his advisers.

Heck’s comments made the case for export controls on the sale of AI chips to China. She repeatedly defended Anthropic as having a long history of being motivated by safety concerns and said it’s focused on working with lawmakers to pass new regulations for the technology.

“We do think it’s existential to do this. We do think we have to balance the risk now,” Heck said. “The capabilities are only increasing and increasing at a pace that is accelerating.”
